Katalog Berita (Halaman 47/58)

#2256. Costacurta: "Se uno vuole giocare in club come il Milan deve avere una certa mentalità in tutte le partite, altrimenti non può farne parte"

L'ex difensore rossonero Alessandro Costacurta ha rilasciato queste parole alla Gazzetta dello Sport sul Milan di Ruben Amorim che sta avendo alti e bassi come la brutta sconfitta contro il Ferencvaros in Europa League pochi giorni dopo la grande vittoria nel derby contro l'Inter: "Credo che ci siano dei anche dei limiti tecnici. È chiaro che però risaltano ancora di più quando non c'è l'impegno e l'attitudine caratteriale. Questo è stato sorprendente perché si arrivava da una vittoria meravigliosa nel derby e quindi quella era veramente la prova per capire se era una squadra che poteva crescere immediatamente oppure bisognava aspettare. Credo che quella sconfitta in casa in Europa abbia confermato che è una squadra che deve migliorare sotto l'aspetto della concentrazione. Siccome ci sono dei limiti tecnici, se emergono anche quelli caratteriali il Milan è una squadra che perde in casa contro il Ferencváros.

Amorim? Io credo che lui sia una persona che possa fare bene. Io ho sempre dato poca importanza sinceramente agli allenatori, nel senso che io credo che ogni giocatore abbia uno spirito e un carattere che deve tirare fuori. Se uno vuole appartenere a una squadra come Milan, Juve, Manchester City, Paris Saint-Germain deve avere una certa mentalità in tutte le partite, altrimenti non può farne parte. E io non ho mai criticato le scelte di Amorim, perché io credo che il Milan abbia tanti giocatori che possono giocare titolari. Quindi io ho soltanto espresso una critica verso i giocatori, mai contro Amorim".

#2254. Named: Premier League team of the season so far as Erling Haaland, THREE Chelsea players and a surprise addition from Sunderland make the cut

Published: 02:00 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 04:56 EST, 14 November 2026

The international break has rolled back around and with it a chance to take stock of the Premier League season so far.

The first ten games of the new campaign have thrown up a few surprises – none of three  promoted teams find themselves in the drop zone at this stage and the race for Europe is wide open with teams such as Brighton and Everton excelling.

Here is a look at the players who have defined the opening weeks as Daily Mail Sport, in collaboration with stats gurus Sofascore, compile our team of the season so far...

Many will be surprised to see the Argentine's name here instead of Arsenal's David Raya or Brighton's Bart Verbruggen, but despite Chelsea's defensive woes it is their £7million summer signing that makes the cut.

Martinez has been out for the last three games after sustaining a nasty head injury away at Everton but his average match rating remains the highest out of all the division's shot-stoppers.

A look at the stats tells you why. Despite only keeping one clean sheet so far, Chelsea's new No1 has prevented 1.64 goals, had 13 high claims and 0 errors leading to goals.

The big man has also looked extremely competent with the ball at his feet, something that Blues keepers have struggled with in previous years, and has even created three chances from his own box so far this season.

Emiliano Martinez has been out for three weeks with a head injury he sustained at Everton but has still done enough to make our team

There was always going to have to be at least one of this Brighton team in our XI. We all knew they were an excellent outfit coming into the season but perhaps even Fabian Hurzeler  may not have envisaged his side sitting second after ten games.

The linchpin of this side has of course been their skipper, Lewis Dunk. A local boy who came through the ranks at Brighton and has spent virtually his entire career at the club, he continues to impress at 34 years of age.

Dunk has played in nine of Brighton's ten games this season looking solid in each, leading his side to six wins and keeping a clean sheet in each victory. And his personal defensive stats make for excellent reading as well – he has won 22 aerial duels and registered 31 recoveries already this season.

But there are some things that can't be quantified, such as Dunk's impact on the  Brighton dressing room and the guidance he gives such a young squad which must be immense – after all, he is a year older than his own manager.

Next up is another old school English centre-half who has captained his team to an excellent start to the season.

The big man is rolling back the years as the Toffees look to push for Europe

In recent years the Toffees have become far more familiar with the bottom of the table than the top but at present are making a serious push for the European places and are currently in sixth place, level on points with fifth.

And the 33-year-old has been vital to David Moyes's new system, providing stability and strength to a defence that has conceded just ten goals – with only Arsenal (five), Brighton (seven) and Leeds (eight) conceding fewer.

Again similar to Dunk, Tarkowski's stats show the veteran's ability to adapt to the demands of the modern game, having 108 line-breaking passes, creating four chances and one big chance so far this season.

The skipper has also come up trumps in close games, bagging a crucial goal in a 1-1 draw at Bournemouth and getting an assist in the 1-0 win over Ipswich.

Completing the back three is the only one out under 30, but is also the man with the highest average match rating in this team.

Considering Tottenham's defensive record this season, one of their defenders making it in may come as a bit of a shock but anyone that has watched the north Londoners this season will know that 26-year-old Van Hecke is hardly the reason for their woes.

The Dutchman has been magnificent since moving from Brighton and reuniting with his old boss Roberto De Zerbi, playing every single minute of the Premier League season so far.

Van Hecke epitomises the modern centre-half, having the second most one-line breaking passes (162), the most two-line breaking passes (37) and the most passes into the final third (138) out of any player in the league – and has even bagged two goals for Spurs as they have started to pick up some form.

Despite Sunderland's poor start, the Black Cats' skipper anchors our midfield with the highest average match rating in his position this campaign. Most would have been expecting Pascal Gross to take this position in an XI such as this considering his eight goals and assists and all-round stellar showing this season.

Xhaka is a surprise entry considering Sunderland's form but the stats tell us that the skipper is still performing

But the boffins have Xhaka here instead and the numbers show why. The Swiss international has excelled in a number of areas despite Sunderland's faltering start having the second-most passes into the final third (132) and the joint most line-breaking passes into the box (21).

Moving onto the midfield, we have perhaps the most electrifying winger in the league  this season.

Manchester City have tailed off with three defeats on the spin but Jeremy Doku still remains a major source of headaches for the league's full-backs and a full-time entertainer for us viewers.

When he first joined the league the Belgian was criticised for a lack of consistency but recently he appears to have put that all behind him. Doku does only have one goal and one assist this season, but that does not tell the full story.

He has completed the most dribbles in the league this season (27), won nearly 60 per cent of his duels and has created 4.25xG while on the pitch.

He also provided us with arguably the performance of the season so far when he changed the game off the bench away at Liverpool, scoring a goal-of-the-season contender to down the Reds.

The first and only man from the champions and league leaders to get into our team is Bukayo Saka.

Saka appears to be getting back to his best as the champions get off to an excellent start in their title defence

It was always going to be hard for the man the fans call 'Starboy' to keep up his form from last season but in actual fact his desire to bring more silverware to the Emirates appears more prevalent than ever.

We all know what he can do going forward and the Englishman has netted three goals in the league, but this year he has improved his defensive game massively, winning 43 duels, 11 tackles and registering 23 recoveries already.

Saka has struggled with his fitness for the past year or so and although he has played their first seven Premier League games, has been on the sidelines since mid-October with a thigh injury.

Despite a testing start to the season, Chelsea are the team with the most players to make the list – though few will quibble with this man's inclusion.

Morgan Rogers proved himself to be a special talent at Aston Villa and there won't be many Chelsea fans doubting the wisdom of paying £117million for his services after his flying start.

Morgan Rogers has been a revelation at the bridge thus far, scoring six goals in all competitions and assisting five more

The Englishman has lit up Stamford Bridge with six goals and five assists in all competitions and has instantly formed a deadly front three with best friend Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro.

The Blues have struggled for form under new manager Xabi Alonso but no criticism can be laid at the feet of Rogers who will hope his goals can bring some much-needed consistency to west London.

Completing the midfield is a man who is finally getting his flowers after months of quality and consistency. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall is one of the many reasons Everton fans are excited for the first time in a while.

The Englishman became an instant fan favourite at the Hill Dickinson after moving from Chelsea last year but this season has gone up a gear in every way, running  games from start to finish with surgical passing, clever dribbling and an incredible work rate.

Only seven players have covered more ground in the league than his 101km (63 miles), and he has also contributed three goals and an assist – as well as delivering a magnificent 79 defensive contributions. His spot in this team could not be more deserved.

Going into the strike-force these next two names are simply must haves, and the first of the two is the mercurial Joao Pedro.

Joao Pedro has the best goals and assists ratio to games in the league with eight in six games

After an excellent debut season in blue the Brazilian took the risk of taking on the infamously cursed Chelsea No9 shirt. But it appears to have only spurred him on further as he has enjoyed a  stellar start to the campaign in front of goal.

It only took him two minutes to get on the score sheet this season in Chelsea's opening game away to Fulham and he just hasn't stopped scoring since.

Pedro has five goals and three assists in just six Premier League games and has become a menace for opposition defences. Unfortunately for gaffer Xabi Alonso his side have been unable to match that consistency, having won five, drawn one and lost four in the league.

But the Spaniard will hope to have his star man back soon – in the six games Pedro has managed to play this season the Blues have lost just one.

It would not be an elite Premier League XI without this man in it.

Even with all the controversy surrounding Manchester City, Erling Haaland manages to roar on and continue scoring at an alarming rate. It is yet another season where he props up the Premier League goal scoring table with nine in ten games.

For a  City side in transition away from a decade under Pep Guardiola Haaland's goals this season have been so crucial in smoothing the process and getting important wins.

The big Norwegian has bagged winners against rivals Manchester United, Ipswich and Coventry as well as netting the vital opener in their 3-0 win at Anfield. Yet again,  he is proving he is the ultimate goal machine.

#2252. Lazio-Lecce, Leite può ritrovare Doekhi: Provstgaard verso il riposo

Sutalo rischia almeno due mesi di stop; per Tavares, Gattuso prepara Pedraza sulla corsia sinistra.

Diogo Leite è destinato a sostituire l'infortunato Sutalo nella difesa della Lazio già contro il Lecce. Secondo quanto riportato da TUTTOmercatoWEB, Gennaro Gattuso deve modificare l'assetto anche per lo stop di Tavares: sulla sinistra il posto dell'ex Arsenal sarà preso da Pedraza.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Al centro della difesa potevano esserci dubbi, ma le indicazioni arrivate dal campo portano a Leite. Sutalo rischia di restare fuori per almeno due mesi. A Formello si spera che la lesione muscolare del croato, ex Ajax, sia meno grave del previsto, anche se i segnali degli ultimi giorni non sono positivi.

L'assenza del difensore pesa sulle scelte per il Lecce. Gattuso ha però mostrato piena fiducia nel portoghese e si prepara ad affidargli il posto di Sutalo.

Accanto a Leite potrebbe giocare Doekhi. Contro i salentini si ricomporrebbe così la coppia di centrali già vista all'Union Berlino. Provstgaard, invece, potrebbe osservare un turno di riposo dopo gli impegni con la Danimarca.

Per Leite sarebbe un'occasione per trovare più spazio dopo un avvio di stagione dal minutaggio limitato. Il difensore è arrivato a inizio settembre a parametro zero, subito dopo la chiusura del mercato. Ha raccolto sei presenze ed è rimasto in panchina soltanto contro Venezia e Juventus.

Dopo il malore e le settimane di stop, Vincent Kompany guarda con ottimismo al suo ritorno in campo con il Bayern Monaco.

#2248. Italia Femminile, le convocate di Soncin per il turno decisivo dei playoff: c'è anche una rossonera

(ANSA) - ROMA, 19 NOV - L'ultimo ostacolo verso il terzo Mondiale di calcio consecutivo per le azzurre è la Finlandia. Sono 29 le convocate della nazionale di Andrea Soncin per la doppia sfida del secondo e decisivo turno dei playoff, in programma il 1° dicembre a Helsinki e il 5 a Taranto. In palio ci sarà il biglietto aereo per il Brasile, dove dal 24 giugno al 25 luglio del 2027 si disputerà la decima edizione del torneo iridato. Le novità sono rappresentate dalle centrocampiste Moraca e Santi, alla prima convocazione in Nazionale maggiore come l'attaccante Distefano. Tornano invece in gruppo De Rita, già chiamata per due amichevoli nel 2024, e insieme a lei anche Linari e Bonfantini.

Appuntamento a Coverciano da martedì 24 novembre. L'Italia si è aggiudicata sei dei 14 precedenti, tra cui l'ultimo il 16 luglio 2024: un netto 4-0 ottenuto al 'Druso' di Bolzano (reti di Beccari, Giugliano, Cambiaghi e autorete di Nyström) che permise alle azzurre di festeggiare insieme ai propri tifosi il pass per l'Europeo. Di seguito l'elenco delle convocate: Portieri: Rachele Baldi (Roma), Francesca Durante (Como 1907), Laura Giuliani (Stoccarda); Difensori: Elisa Bartoli (Inter), Valentina Bergamaschi (Roma), Lisa Boattin (Houston Dash), Aurora De Rita (Como 1907), Lucia Di Guglielmo (Washington Spirit), Martina Lenzini (Juventus), Elena Linari (London City Lionesses), Elisabetta Oliviero (Roma), Martina Rosucci (Juventus), Cecilia Salvai (Juventus), Angelica Soffia (Milan); Centrocampiste: Arianna Caruso (Real Madrid), Giulia Dragoni (Chelsea), Manuela Giugliano (Roma), Giuseppina Moraca (Como 1907), Irene Santi (Inter), Eva Schatzer (Juventus), Emma Severini (Fiorentina); Attaccanti: Agnese Bonfantini (Como 1907), Michela Cambiaghi (Inter), Sofia Cantore (Washington Spirit), Gaia Distefano (Parma), Cristiana Girelli (Bay FC), Benedetta Glionna (Inter), Martina Piemonte (Roma), Elisa Polli (Inter). (ANSA).

#2246. Hernanes: «la Lazio ha il 15% di portare a casa il campionato». Inter favorita

Il Profeta ricorda il suo sogno di vincere a Roma ed elogia Gattuso, Zaccagni e Frattesi nella squadra capolista.

Hernanes assegna alla Lazio il 15% di possibilità di vincere lo scudetto, pur considerando l’Inter la squadra più forte. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, L’ex centrocampista, soprannominato «Profeta», si dice emozionato nel vedere i biancocelesti primi in classifica e riconosce nella squadra la mentalità di Gattuso.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Per descriverla, Hernanes sceglie un vino che produce in Piemonte: «La Lazio di Gattuso è come un Grignolino, un rosso che produco sulle colline di Asti e di Monferrato, in Piemonte. Un vino romantico. Quando lo bevi, ti viene da sorridere. E mi capita di farlo ogni volta che guardo questa Lazio, prima in classifica con pieno merito». Produce vino da una decina d’anni e nelle Langhe ha il suo campo base, chiamato «Ca’ del profeta».

Il primato ha sorpreso anche lui: «Non me l’aspettavo, ma s’è creata una bella magia». Alla domanda sul titolo richiama l’impresa del Leicester in Premier League, poi dà una percentuale: «Io dico che la Lazio ha il 15% di portare a casa il campionato. Anche se la più forte resta sempre l’Inter».

Hernanes distingue l’emozione dal tifo: è affezionato anche agli altri club in cui ha giocato, ma ricorda che, al suo arrivo a Roma, dichiarò di voler vincere il campionato. Gli risposero che la Lazio lottava per l’Europa; lui, racconta, combatté quella mentalità. «Sognavo di vincere e di lottare per lo scudetto. Vederla lassù mi emoziona».

Nella squadra Hernanes rivede il carattere dell’allenatore: «Questa Lazio gli somiglia: è come se in campo ci fossero undici Rino. È riuscito a trasmettere la sua mentalità alla squadra. La voglia di azzannare ogni caviglia, lottare su ogni pallone, dare tutto senza risparmiarsi mai. Vedo la sua fame, la sua voglia». Da avversario affrontò Gattuso due volte e dice di averlo sempre stimato per l’onestà e il rispetto con cui giocava.

Tra i biancocelesti cita Zaccagni, che secondo i dati da lui studiati crea più occasioni di chiunque altro, e poi Mandas, Belahyane, Provstgaard, Floriani Mussolini e Frattesi. È soprattutto Frattesi, a suo giudizio, a rispecchiare il calcio di Gattuso: nella corsa fatta contro il Napoli prima del gol Hernanes vede ciò che serve per sognare lo scudetto. A Taylor, ribattezzato «profeta», riconosce intelligenza tattica, senso del gol e qualità tecniche. Considera inoltre l’infortunio di Nuno Tavares un duro colpo: per caratteristiche fisiche e stile di gioco lo ritiene insostituibile.

Hernanes non crede che i tifosi tornerebbero allo stadio se a marzo la Lazio fosse ancora in quella posizione. Cita la scaramanzia e il rapporto con il presidente, augurandosi che la situazione si risolva perché la squadra merita uno stadio pieno.

Tra i ricordi biancocelesti sceglie i gol nei derby, la Coppa Italia del 26 maggio e le punizioni segnate con entrambi i piedi. Soprattutto, però, gli è rimasta una frase rivoltagli da un tifoso: «non te ne annà, profe’…». Racconta che, dopo quel pomeriggio a Formello, ricevette circa diecimila messaggi dai laziali e cercò di rispondere a tutti. Per lo scudetto indica ancora l’Inter come favorita e invita a fare attenzione anche alla Roma. Di Nico Paz dice che è più forte di lui: «Un fenomeno».

#2245. RIATH AL-SAMARRAI: I'm told control over transfers was key to Mauricio Pochettino taking Man United job. It seems they finally have a manager bullish enough to hold Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Jason Wilcox to account

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 09:10 EST, 14 November 2026

It only happened once. But if you search for it, there is footage. The date was February 23, 2000 and the place was the old Wembley Stadium. England 0-0 Argentina, the kind of friendly best forgotten, except for a single line of trivia.

Of all the games played by Jason Wilcox and Mauricio Pochettino, this was the sole example of them sharing a pitch. Wilcox was given the full 90 at a point when Kevin Keegan was low on options for the left wing and Pochettino came on with 35 minutes on the clock and kicked a few people.

He was good at kicking people, Pochettino. He flattened Paul Scholes once, then he nudged over David Beckham and twice he got stuck into Emile Heskey. But Wilcox was in a safe zone on the other side of the field that night. While Pochettino indulged his hobby, Wilcox kept out of harm’s way.

We might ask at this juncture if either of them ever changed their spots. But it’s more interesting to ponder what comes next, now they have been pitched together again at Manchester United.

United needed a big bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one. Wilcox’s preference? Well, United’s director of hopeless football quite fancied Eddie Howe, according to the whispers, and Howe is far from a shrinking violet, but he’s not Pochettino. And Pochettino certainly isn’t Carrick.

Pochettino won’t drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run. And he won’t have the same patience for incompetence from those below or above.

Manchester United needed a big bull to replace Michael Carrick and they have got one in Mauricio Pochettino

Pochettino is not the sort of manager to drive to work for three days straight while knowing his race is run, like Carrick did this week

With any luck, United knew this when they reached an agreement that was a decade in the making. If they did, it would demonstrate some self-awareness at last, because United have badly needed the right blend of bruiser and diplomat in that seat.

They have cried out for someone who isn’t too nice, too loyal, too whiny or too undermined by their own shortcomings to have the kind of rucks that are needed for change. By that logic, United may have invited their own worst enemy to dinner, or their best chance of a solution.

There have been few managerial appointments in recent years as inherently fascinating as this one. That instinct is partly driven by the thought it has all arrived a touch late – when United favoured Ole Gunnar Solskjaer to replace Jose Mourinho, it was a sliding-door moment for all parties.

But there’s another way of viewing this and that comes from the opposite angle. Maybe this is the perfect time, based on the qualifications needed to operate within the modern version of United.

There is no doubt that Pochettino has lost some of his sheen since his masterful handling of Daniel Levy at Tottenham, but what did he gain? He managed the vastest collection of footballing egos at PSG, worked under a convoluted tier of meddlers in the madhouse of Chelsea and was confronted by presidential interference in his time with the US national team at the World Cup.

Two schools of thought can exist here. One is that he failed to tear up any trees in each of those assignments. But the other talks to the point we are making: United require a manager who can navigate their unique brand of chaos and the new guy knows the dance.

Pochettino won’t ever thank Donald Trump for the Folarin Balogun fiasco in the summer, but Sir Jim Ratcliffe would have to work awfully hard to cause him a more uncomfortable press conference.

The scale of Pochettino’s challenge is obvious. In the micro, that means applying a playing style built on hard running to a squad that jogged its way to embarrassing statistics under Carrick. In the macro, it will be his challenge with Wilcox and a recruitment team that effectively cost Carrick his job.

Pochettino has had plenty to deal with as USA coach, not least the meddling of Donald Trump

Pochettino has the authority to challenge (above, from left) Sir Jim Ratcliffe, Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox over United's failing transfer policy

Talking to one of Pochettino’s former colleagues on Friday, the expectation is that greater control over transfers will have been a key tenet of those negotiations with United.

As predictable as that might sound, it was a huge bone of contention for him at Chelsea and United’s failures in this area are clear. Time will tell if any promises are honoured.

But Pochettino has got what he wanted and pursued. His desire for the post has never been disguised, which can be mapped as a trail of breadcrumbs from that bottle of red he once shared with Sir Alex Ferguson all the way up to carefully planted mentions of the club in gatherings with media.

There were some acts of reassurance necessary for the final step, of course, and doubtless it will sting to leave the US - his farewell tears on Friday showed as much. But not enough to inspire a second thought.

To look back over Pochettino’s other stints in England, one main memory stands out from his time at Tottenham and I’ve cited it in this space previously.

It traces to September 2016, when Pochettino was on the rise and had a game approaching against Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City. In attempting to coax a decent line in the press conference, a few of us killed time before his arrival by digging up old footage of Pochettino’s Espanyol beating Barcelona, when he and Guardiola were on opposing sides.

Within the clip was an unexpected gem, because Pochettino murdered the Brazilian Ronaldo in a challenge. He took the ball, sure, but demolished the man, too, and his boot ended up shoulder-high. We were watching this when Pochettino wandered over and requested a replay – when it was shown, he laughed maniacally.

As a player, he always saw the value in a good reducer. And it’s a trait that might well be needed at United. If Wilcox and the other cronies upstairs don’t up their game, they might find that Carrington offers fewer hiding places than the old Wembley.

Pochettino's fondness for the USA job was apparent by his farewell tears on Friday

Was Tom Brady ever in the Blues' building?

Tom Brady has left Birmingham, but was he ever really there? Across three years, he attended only four games.

The club is on a steep upward trajectory and there is no doubt that the Brady association helped on their commercial side.

But I recall speaking to one Blues shareholder a couple of seasons back, and after attempting to establish some tangible detail about their star investor’s contribution, there was a period of silence. When I asked how often Brady might dial into meetings, there was laughter.

In this era of celebrity ownership of our football clubs, it’s easy to get blinded by a famous name. And easier still to get drawn in by suggestions of expertise that they have carried over from a different space.

But in the vast majority of cases, they are little more than mascots without the costume.

Tom Brady makes a rare appearance at a Birmingham match in 2025

Great delivery from Cummins - but it's not over yet

Pat Cummins stood for 70 minutes on Thursday and answered questions about Sandpapergate.

The Australia captain refused to budge, both from the microphone and his position that Usman Khawaja was incorrect in his claim that the entire team was in on the plot to cheat against South Africa in 2018.

It’s hard to know what was more impressive – Cummins’ commitment to answering every question, or his delusion in believing that it would be the last time he discusses it.

Hernanes, ex centrocampista brasiliano di Inter e Lazio, ha rilasciato un’intervista ai microfoni de’ La Gazzetta dello Sport.

L’ex nerazzurro ha trattato alcuni temi caldi del calcio italiano tra cui la lotta Scudetto e la sfida a distanza tra due delle squadra in cui ha militato, proprio Inter e Lazio.

"Anche me. Non me l’aspettavo, ma s’è creata una bella magia".

La domanda ce la giochiamo subito: può vincere lo scudetto?

"Gliene faccio un’altra io: perché non può vincerlo? Mi è venuto in mente il Leicester: non ci credeva nessuno, e invece ha vinto il titolo diventando la Cenerentola della Premier League. Io dico che la Lazio ha il 15% di portare a casa il campionato. Anche se la più forte resta sempre l’Inter".

"L’Inter. Marotta e tutta la dirigenza sono un punto di riferimento. La squadra è completa, forte ovunque, solida. Dopo la batosta del derby ho avuto l’impressione che la squadra abbia ripreso a girare a pieno ritmo. Come se avessero pensato “ok, ora si fa sul serio”. Occhio anche alla Roma, comunque".

"Nico Paz, ma è più forte di me… non scherziamo. Un fenomeno".

#2238. Lazio e nazionali, da Mandas a Isaksen: Gattuso fa i conti con gli stop

Il portiere esordisce da titolare con la Grecia e l’esterno serve un assist; Tavares, Sutalo e Marusic sono fermi.

La Lazio ritrova cinque calciatori impiegati dal primo minuto con le rispettive nazionali: Mandas, Dele-Bashiru, Belahyane, Provstgaard e Isaksen. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Alle soddisfazioni della sosta si affianca ora la gestione delle energie. In vista del Lecce, Gattuso ragiona su turnover e modulo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Lunedì Mandas ha festeggiato l’esordio da titolare con la Grecia, mantenendo la porta inviolata contro la Serbia. Martedì è toccato a Dele-Bashiru e Belahyane partire dal primo minuto, rispettivamente con Nigeria e Marocco.

Provstgaard e Isaksen hanno giocato entrambi tutti i 99 minuti con la Danimarca. Il difensore ha retto l’urto, mentre Isaksen ha servito un assist. In Nations League, però, i danesi si sono fatti rimontare dalla Norvegia.

Come osserva Il Messaggero, a Formello le presenze nelle selezioni sono motivo d’orgoglio. I calciatori biancocelesti hanno ritrovato spazio e attenzione: alle convocazioni sono seguite le titolarità e, nel caso di Isaksen, anche un assist.

Per il club è una soddisfazione legata al riconoscimento sul campo dei propri giocatori, dopo un periodo in cui il loro valore di mercato era stato spesso al centro dell’attenzione. Il rovescio riguarda il rientro: le nazionali restituiscono i calciatori alla Lazio proprio mentre riprendono gli impegni. È in questo quadro che Gattuso valuta le scelte per il Lecce.

#2237. Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026

Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal. Morgan Rogers appeared in just 217 for Bournemouth, then of the Championship. The pair are the same school age. Yet, back then, one was a young man at the very top of the game, the other was a boy wondering where, and how, he would ever get a game.

In the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby. They were on very different flight paths.

Today, the ascent of Rogers compares with, dare we say it, the gradual descent of Saka. His supporters will contest that trajectory. They can point to his two goals for England in Croatia last month, his hat-trick in the 6-4 World Cup bronze-medal victory over France and, of course, his Premier League winner’s medal. Their argument has merit, as does any that defends a player of such talent.

Except, this is not about ability. It is about durability. It is about mileage and the fear that, at 25 years old, a near 400 career games are weighing heavy. Rogers, quite remarkably, has played 10,000 fewer Premier League minutes. He is, to borrow horse-racing parlance, unexposed and open to improvement.

Until three years ago, this was Saka. He started 87 consecutive Premier League games for Arsenal, a club record, and was getting better season on season - seven, 12, 15 and 20 were his goals tallies from 2021 to 2024. He was both the present and future of the England team.

Bukayo Saka's starting spot in the England XI is now under serious threat ahead of Euro 2028

England are flourishing with Chelsea's Morgan Rogers (right) occupying the right-hand side

And yet now, increasingly among those who obverse and are close to the England camp - including, you suspect, Thomas Tuchel - there is a feeling of Saka’s presumed starting jersey being under serious threat. In fact, you wonder if the threat has already passed. Does the position on the right of England’s forward line, with a view to Euro 2028, now belong to Rogers?

This, it should be said, is as much about the exceptional development of Rogers, who will again start on the right here in Spain on Sunday night. But there is another, more uncomfortable possibility, and that is of Saka’s very best days belonging to those North London derbies of yesterday, not tomorrow. He is currently injured with a thigh strain and faces several more weeks on the sidelines.

I was in the room with Tuchel at the World Cup pre-camp in Florida when he revealed, to some surprise, ’Bukayo is just not there yet. Some things are missing’. We had assumed Saka was fit after arranging private sessions in the wake of the Champions League final. The head coach, however, said it would be ‘very unlikely’ that Saka, nursing Achilles discomfort, would be able to start and finish all of England’s matches, and so it proved. He did not start and finish any before the France kick-about, a match that should have been played at Miami Beach, not Miami Stadium.

In the days prior to the semi-final against Argentina, Saka told Tuchel and medical staff he was ready to start. Tuchel went with Rogers on the right and Saka was an unused substitute. After his treble three days later, Saka spoke of his frustration with his playing time in North America.

Throughout the tournament, Tuchel rejected the idea of the Arsenal man being ‘the saviour’, as it was put to him by one colleague following the group-stage goalless draw with Ghana.

‘I’m not engaging in that,’ he told us. ‘It’s not like Bukayo comes back and everything is solved.’

And Tuchel was right. Saka did a lot of good - three assists in the tournament proper - but it felt like he was existing in moments, much like at Euro 2024. Gone was that whiplash speed taking him through defensive lines, the drag and dribble that defenders knew was coming but could do little about. Club-mate Noni Madueke had that explosion, just not Saka’s end product. Combine the two and we had a player. It was why, come the semis, Tuchel went with Rogers.

Recurring injuries and setbacks have plagued the Arsenal winger over the past few seasons

He was once viewed as England's present and future - but has suffered from a gradual decline

To revisit our Daily Mail Sport tournament ratings, in which Saka scored 6/10, we recorded: ‘Fitness issues should offer some context, but this was a version of Saka unrecognisable from the player we thought was up there with Kane and Bellingham when it came to being a game-changer. He did provide three assists, including a lovely cross for the opener in Mexico, but never appeared to fully trust his body. Has a bit to prove when back to full fitness.’

Will he ever, though, regain a consistent level of fitness, strength and sharpness that allows him to impact - again, consistently - like he once did? Just last week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted the club were struggling to identify the underlying reason for injuries which total double figures in three years.

‘We have openly discussed a lot of things with him to understand what could possibly have gone wrong,’ said Arteta. ‘But the reality probably is that unfortunately we don’t know.’

Saka, to return to horse racing, has the form in the book, but that is the concern. There is, perhaps, too much form at too young an age, especially when coupled with a game reliant on acceleration and intensity.

Rogers himself still has a lot to prove, not least because of his £117million transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea in the summer. With that, though, he has grown. That much was evident by him taking centre stage against Croatia on Thursday night despite the presence of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham. Previously, you suspected Rogers was waiting for the leading men to hand him his script.

His tendency to come infield will suit Tuchel, too. Kane the quarterback, as we saw at Wembley, leaves a space to populate and exploit. Rogers had more touches in the penalty area than any other player, including the one for his opening goal. And if Anthony Gordon, on the opposite flank, is the one with chalk on his boots, Rogers muddying his in the goalmouth is what the team needs.

Meanwhile, Rogers has hit top gear at Chelsea and become a key man under Thomas Tuchel

This debate, Saka versus Rogers, is not one that should keep Tuchel awake at night. It is a nice problem to have - the hope that Saka will return to his best, the expectation that Rogers is still to realise his.

On Sunday, at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Rogers has another opportunity to further his claims. He has come a long way since a drab Wednesday night at Peterborough’s London Road in 2021. It is, though, the distance yet travelled that is most exciting.

#2234. Brasile, arrestata l'ex calciatrice Gabi Morais: è accusata di narcotraffico e riciclaggio

Gabi Morais, ex calciatrice della nazionale brasiliana femminile, è stata arrestata martedì nell'ambito dell'Operazione Liquidazione, un blitz della Polizia Civile del Ceará contro il narcotraffico e il riciclaggio di denaro legati al Comando Vermelho, una delle principali organizzazioni criminali del Brasile.

Secondo l'inchiesta, riportata dal Diário do Nordeste, Morais avrebbe ricoperto un ruolo centrale e strategico nelle attività di riciclaggio e nel traffico di droga dell'organizzazione. Fonti della polizia citate dal quotidiano riferiscono che l'ex calciatrice avrebbe negoziato la vendita di stupefacenti nel quartiere Lagamar, a Fortaleza, mentre il fratello João Paulo Carneiro de Morais, conosciuto come "JP Lagamar", si sarebbe occupato della distribuzione in altri quartieri. Il padre, João Bosco da Rocha, soprannominato "João Presinha", sarebbe invece collegato ad attività in altri Stati del Paese, ma non è stato arrestato durante questa operazione.

Uno dei presunti sistemi utilizzati per riciclare il denaro sarebbe il bar Adega Revoada GM, situato sempre a Lagamar, dove Morais organizzava feste praticamente ogni due settimane. In passato, proprio per questi eventi, aveva avuto problemi con la giustizia a causa di un reato ambientale legato all'utilizzo degli impianti audio. La vicenda aveva portato a una multa di 6.484 real, circa 1.100 dollari, a favore di un ente impegnato nella tutela ambientale.

L'inchiesta ha anche precedenti legati alla famiglia. João Bosco da Rocha era già stato identificato dalla Polizia Civile come uno dei principali trafficanti della zona di Lagamar. Nel gennaio 2014, all'età di 48 anni, era stato arrestato dal Dipartimento antidroga (Denarc) al termine di due mesi di indagini, quando era considerato il principale narcotrafficante della regione. In quell'occasione erano state fermate anche altre sei persone, tra cui il genero.

Secondo quella precedente indagine, l'uomo avrebbe guidato una banda armata sospettata di essere responsabile di omicidi a Lagamar e nei quartieri vicini, come Aerolândia e Tancredo Neves. Gli obiettivi sarebbero stati trafficanti rivali e consumatori che avevano accumulato debiti con l'organizzazione.

Morais, 32 anni e originaria dello Stato del Ceará, lo scorso giugno aveva pubblicato un video in cui si mostrava durante un allenamento. Fino a febbraio di quest'anno aveva giocato nell'Internacional di Porto Alegre, prima di interrompere il contratto consensualmente con il club.

In precedenza aveva vestito la maglia del Corinthians, conquistando due campionati brasiliani, una Supercoppa brasiliana e una Copa Libertadores. Aveva inoltre giocato nelle selezioni Under 20 e nella nazionale maggiore, con cui ha collezionato quattro presenze.

Juventus, Brentford e Bournemouth seguono il 24enne, che non è stato convocato con l’Olanda e non intende lasciare Roma.

Kenneth Taylor ha ribadito a Gattuso di voler restare alla Lazio a gennaio. Il centrocampista conosce l’interesse di Juventus, Brentford e Bournemouth, ma la sua volontà coincide con quella del club biancoceleste. CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il 24enne non sembra distratto dalle sirene di mercato. ha confermato a Gattuso la propria intenzione di non muoversi nella sessione invernale, nonostante l’attenzione dei tre club.

Alla ripresa del lavoro c’è anche Frattesi. Rientrato affaticato da San Siro, dove ha segnato contro la Francia, il centrocampista ha subito corso e lavorato con il gruppo.

#2229. Fiorentina, l'ex Pruzzo su Beto: "A gennaio lo manderei a giocare, è inadatto a subentrare"

L'ex attaccante della Fiorentina, Roberto Pruzzo, è intervenuto a Lady Radio analizzando anche lo scarso rendimento di Beto in questa prima parte di stagione coi gigliati. Di seguito il suo pensiero sull'ex Udinese ed Everton.

"Non ho speranze di vederlo titolare nel breve-medio termine, perché è lontano da una forma accettabile. Anche se farà un gol, non bisogna illuderci, non si sbloccherà in questo modo. Per me non è infatti l'attaccante adatto per subentrare a gara in corso e incidere sulla partita", ha dichiarato lo storico bomber. "D'altronde Vanoli ha scelto giustamente Pellegrino come punta titolare, perché anche se non è il migliore d'Europa fa il suo. Per questo a gennaio proverei a cercare una soluzione diversa per Beto che ha bisogno di rilanciarsi, ma a Firenze non avrebbe continuità. Lo manderei in prestito a giocare, così magari si ritroverà", ha concluso.

Acquistato dall'Everton per oltre 18 milioni di euro, Beto finora ha realizzato solamente un assist, e zero gol, in dieci presenze con la divisa della Fiorentina. In totale, ha giocato 206 minuti.

#2228. Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026

In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.

Point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss. But here we are.

It’s 30 years to the day since Van Vossen missed an open goal for Rangers during a crucial Old Firm clash at Celtic Park. Leading 1-0 and with less than seven minutes remaining, the Dutch forward had a chance to seal all three points for the nine-in-a-row-chasing Light Blues. Instead, he blazed over with the goal at his mercy.

In the decades since, the spurned chance has become the benchmark by which all other misses have been measured. ‘Sure, it was bad — but was it “Van Vossen” bad?’

The man himself has seldom spoken about the events of that powder keg of a night. Until now. Living the quiet life in rural Holland, Van Vossen has given Daily Mail Sport a full account of his professional nadir.

‘I mostly remember being mad at Jorg [Albertz],’ he says. ‘I was seriously p***** off with him. Paul Gascoigne played a pass inside to me and I clipped a first-time ball in behind the Celtic defence, who were pressing high. If Jorg had just left it, I was one-on-one with the goalie and I would have fancied my chances.

Rangers striker Peter van Vossen sends the ball skywards in a crucial Old Firm clash in 1996

‘I also thought there was a chance he might have been offside, so when you see me running through and stretching out my arms, that’s not me telling him that we’re through; that’s me telling him to leave it and get out of the way!

‘Anyway, he didn’t, I continued my run, he passed it to me and, because I was still livid when the ball arrived at me, I wasn’t paying enough attention. It took a bit of a bobble, I ended up basically hitting it with my shin and, yeah, it unfortunately flew over the bar.’

To his relief, Rangers held on for a 1-0 win to leapfrog their bitter rivals at the top of the table, albeit only after Andy Goram saved a Pierre van Hooijdonk penalty awarded moments after Van Vossen’s horror miss.

‘Walter Smith came up to me in the dressing room afterwards and said, “It’s just as well The Goalie saved that penalty otherwise I’d have f****** killed you!”’ smiles Van Vossen.

‘It was horrible but I can laugh about it now because we won the game. I wish I had scored but I didn’t, so there’s nothing I can do except try to find the humour in it.’

Van Vossen signed for Rangers in January 1996 in a swap deal that saw Oleg Salenko join Istanbulspor. He came with some pedigree, too, having won the Champions League with Ajax in 1995, a year after featuring for the Netherlands on their run to the last eight of the World Cup in the US.

At that time, Rangers, bankrolled by David Murray, were in the throes of a project designed to deliver European glory, while maintaining their dominance of Scottish football. Those two objectives, says Van Vossen, were misaligned.

‘We had a quality group of players that was far better than anything else in Scotland at the time,’ he says. ‘That made us incredibly difficult to beat in the league. But when we went into European games, we were exposed. The lack of competition in the league along with the lifestyles of some of our players was not compatible with taking on champions from other countries.

‘I always felt like we were technically a little behind. Our training usually consisted of a warm-up, a game of football, and a warm-down. That was a big adjustment for me. At Ajax, we played in a system and we worked hard on making sure everybody knew their role. In Scotland, it seemed like there was no real system. You could run anywhere you wanted. I don’t really think I learned anything in my time there.’

That’s not to say he didn’t enjoy his two-and-a-half years in Glasgow. Quite the opposite.

‘I loved playing for Rangers,’ he says. ‘Particularly that second season [1996/97]. I started really well and scored seven or eight goals in the first handful of games. I remember people being quite surprised because I had taken some time to settle. They would joke, “Who are you, Van Vossen’s better twin brother?” But I loved it.’

A dejected Van Vossen can't believe he's missed in a moment that would follow him forever

He reserves particular affection for Walter Smith. ‘He was a fantastic manager and a true gentleman,’ he nods. ‘He helped me through a difficult time in my personal life. When I wasn’t in his team on the weekend, for example, I would ask him if I could go back to the Netherlands to see my children. He always said yes on the condition that I was back in time for training at 10am on Monday.

‘He genuinely cared about his players. I remember Vitesse being interested in bringing me back to Holland and their coach Leo Beenhakker coming to watch me at Ibrox.

‘After the game, he found Walter and said, “We want to sign Peter, but we think £300,000 is too much”. Walter said to him, “Listen to me carefully. We don’t do business like this. First, you and I will go for a lunch, have a respectful chat and only when we’ve got to know each other, that’s when we’ll talk about money”.

‘Walter came to me afterwards and said, “Look, I know you’re not playing as much as you would like but I won’t let you sign for him. This isn’t a good manager and I can’t allow it. You’re one of my players and I care about getting you the right move, not just any move”. I really respected that.’

Van Vossen endured a much more difficult relationship with Smith’s assistant Archie Knox, a man he describes as ‘manipulative’.

‘I didn’t get on with him,’ he says. ‘People talk a lot nowadays about creating a safe space and the right culture in workplaces. To me, Archie didn’t do that. He was always shouting, always right on top of you, in your face, kicking bottles. He behaved like a madman.

Van Vossen scored nine goals in 31 caps for the Netherlands between 1992 and 2000

‘At Ajax, the coaches wanted to know how you were feeling. They understood that being well mentally was as important as being physically fit. Archie wasn’t interested in that. He was always aggressive, but only with the players he didn’t like. He had his favourites. If you weren’t one of them, he made sure you knew all about it.’

Background tensions aside, Van Vossen’s first full season at Ibrox, 1996/97, has assumed a special place in Rangers’ folklore. They finished five points clear of Celtic to equal their rivals’ record of nine consecutive league titles, having laid the foundations with four league wins out of four over Tommy Burns’ side.

Despite his famous miss being the closest he ever came to scoring in an Old Firm clash, Van Vossen insists he relished those occasions.

‘I loved those games,’ he says. ‘The atmosphere, home and away, was unbelievable and the quality of the players on the pitch was outstanding. To be honest, there wasn’t a whole lot of football played. There were lots of mistakes, fights and loads of running. I remember feeling tired after just ten minutes. I wasn’t built for that kind of pace! But they were great to be part of.

‘The week of Old Firm matches, you could feel the pressure building. I remember being in Glasgow city centre one day and I needed a taxi. I waved one down but when it pulled up, the driver must have been a Celtic fan because he raised his middle finger and swore at me before driving away. Whereas, with Rangers taxi drivers, it was the opposite. I honestly think they would have driven me around Scotland for free.

Van Vossen had a spell in charge of Fortuna Sittard but now labels himself a 'house husband'

‘That’s just what football is like in Glasgow. It’s on a whole other level to anything else. I’ve played in big derbies in the Netherlands and Turkey. Believe me, nothing comes close to the Old Firm.’

After finding his playing time limited as Rangers pursued ten-in-a-row, Van Vossen was relieved to learn that his old international manager, Dick Advocaat, would take over from Smith in time for the 1998/99 season. His joy, however, was short-lived when Murray used him as a makeweight in a transfer for Feyenoord midfielder Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

‘David Murray was a brilliant guy, but he made a huge mistake when he tried to sell me to Feyenoord behind the back of Dick Advocaat,’ says Van Vossen. ‘Dick was taking over and he was keen for me to be part of his plans.

‘I remember he was flying from Amsterdam to Glasgow when he phoned me to talk about some of his ideas. I said, “Dick, I’m sorry, but I think I’m joining Feyenoord. The deal is almost done”. He told me to stay put and said that when he got to Glasgow, he and I were going to go and see Murray.

‘I remember Dick said to him, “How can you sell players behind my back? I need to be involved in these conversations”. Murray said, “You’re absolutely right, I apologise”. He handed me a blank cheque and said, “Peter, write down whatever number you want to stay. It’s not a problem”.

‘But I couldn’t do it. I respected him for apologising to Dick, but I had lost confidence in him. I couldn’t play for somebody who would do something like that.

Van Vossen scored 11 goals in his 36 appearances for Rangers between 1996 and 1998

‘I took a 60 per cent drop in wages to join Feyenoord but they were the team I had supported as a boy and I needed to be somewhere I was wanted and where I was being treated with respect.’

Although his spell at Ibrox ended on a slightly sour note, Van Vossen recalls it fondly. ‘It was a family,’ he says. ‘Everybody had a part to play, from the players on the pitch to the ladies in the kitchen. I mean, they were incredible. I remember being on a ferry one time and I got chatting to a truck driver who told me he sold flowers. We had a good conversation and exchanged numbers.

‘When I got back to Glasgow, I got in touch with him and said, “Can you do me a favour? Can you deliver ten bouquets of flowers to Ibrox?” Sure enough, this huge truck pulled up outside the ground one day, with something like ten thousand flowers in the back. They pulled out ten bouquets and delivered them to the ladies in the kitchen. They were delighted, but it was the least I could do. They treated you like one of their own. Like I say, we were one big family.’

These days, the head of that family is one of Van Vossen’s old teammates, Derek McInnes, and he’s backing him to deliver silverware.

Despite carving out a successful career, Van Vossen is remembered primarily for THAT miss

‘I remember Derek well,’ he says. ‘Like me, he didn’t play every game, but he always gave 100 per cent and I expect he’ll be the same as a manager. He’s a people person and I imagine he is a fantastic man-manager. I have no doubt he’ll do a great job.’

Having dabbled in management and punditry since hanging up his boots, Van Vossen now describes himself as a ‘house husband’ who dotes on wife Jojanneke and his stepchildren Sem, Lilly, Madée and Eva. He’s also currently writing his autobiography. The simple pleasures, he insists, are what matter most to him.

‘I don’t need to have lots of expensive things and a certain kind of lifestyle to be a rich man,’ he adds. ‘I’m a rich man because of the memories I have and the good times I enjoyed as a footballer.

‘If I close my eyes, I can still remember what it was like to run onto the pitch at Ibrox in front of 50,000 supporters, and it gives me goosebumps. I am very fortunate to have had that opportunity.’

#2226. Pedraza, chance nella Lazio contro il Lecce: Tavares è fermo

Lo spagnolo cerca spazio sulla fascia sinistra: Gattuso potrà valutarlo anche nelle gare con Torino e Atalanta.

Alfonso Pedraza avrà una chance sulla fascia sinistra della Lazio contro il Lecce, approfittando dello stop di Nuno Tavares. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, Lo spagnolo cerca spazio dopo un avvio difficile: le gare con i salentini, il Torino e l’Atalanta sono tre occasioni per convincere Rino Gattuso, che finora non si è fidato completamente di lui.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

l’obiettivo non è scavalcare Tavares nelle gerarchie, ma guadagnare la fiducia del tecnico e più minuti, anche a partita in corso. Belahyane ha già saputo sfruttare i problemi di Rovella; ora Pedraza può provare a fare altrettanto durante l’assenza del portoghese.

Le due presenze da titolare di Pedraza risalgono entrambe ad agosto. La prima, contro il Mantova in Coppa Italia, è coincisa con il punto più basso della stagione biancoceleste. La seconda è arrivata a Bologna, all’esordio in campionato: in quel caso il risultato è stato diverso grazie a Davide Frattesi.

L’esperienza dello spagnolo a Formello non è dunque cominciata nel modo sperato. Nei 251 minuti giocati in Serie A, però, Pedraza ha servito due assist decisivi: il primo contro il Monza, dopo un buon inserimento, e il secondo contro il Genoa, apparso meno cercato. Entrambi hanno mandato a segno Andrea Pinamonti.

Pinamonti sarà titolare anche sabato pomeriggio all’Olimpico contro il Lecce. La Lazio ha costruito soprattutto a sinistra molte occasioni nel corso della stagione, grazie a Tavares e Zaccagni, ma ora deve fare a meno di entrambi i titolari di quella zona del campo.

Davanti a Pedraza ci sarà Noslin: i due dovranno trovare le giuste misure, almeno nei primi minuti. Per lo spagnolo sarà anche l’occasione di avvicinarsi al rendimento mostrato al Villarreal, dove ha costruito la propria carriera dimostrando di poter giocare a certi livelli.

Pedraza è tra i pochi nuovi acquisti che non sono ancora entrati nelle grazie dei tifosi. In precedenza, le voci su una possibile partenza di Tavares avevano fatto pensare che potesse diventare lui il titolare. Il portoghese è rimasto e ha mostrato un rendimento diverso rispetto agli anni passati, pur dovendo fare i conti ancora con un infortunio.

Una rete pesantissima, decisiva, arrivata nel primo minuto di recupero di una sfida che sembra stregata e che si è trasformata in un incredibile tripudio di gioia. Una rete in cui ci sono tutte le qualità di Marcus Thuram: forza fisica e velocità, tecnica nello stretto, capacità di inquadrare la porta e di calciare indifferentemente con entrambi i piedi, voglia di vincere.

Una rete voluta a ogni costo, costruita da una giocata inesorabile di Tikus, che dopo 90 minuti di lotta ha avuto ancora la forza di scattare in profondità, controllare il pallone e arrivare al limite dell'area sul lato destro. Da lì si è accentrato, ha scambiato nello stretto con Diouf, e dopo aver ricevuto l'appoggio di ritorno si è aggiustato il pallone sul sinistro per calciare. Un rasoterra perfetto, in buca d'angolo, a beffare De Gea sul prima palo. Una rete che ha avviato una rimonta impensabile, che ha regalato al San Siro nerazzurro un pomeriggio indimenticabile.

Il gol di Thuram nell'ottava giornata è stato scelto dai tifosi nerazzurri come il migliore del mese di ottobre: Marcus Thuram vince il premio eFootball Goal of the month con la sua rete contro la Fiorentina!

#2224. Dani Alves e la vita da predicatore: "In carcere ero più felice di quando guadagnavo milioni"

Dani Alves ha condiviso sui social un intervento pubblico nel quale ha raccontato il suo percorso personale, il riavvicinamento alla religione e una riflessione sorprendente sul rapporto tra successo, denaro e felicità.

Durante un incontro con i fedeli, Alves ha spiegato quanto oggi la fede abbia assunto un ruolo centrale nella sua vita. "Mio padre è il padrone dell’oro e dell’argento, quindi non ho bisogno di nulla. Dice che la sua presenza è pienezza di gioia. Io quindi non ho più bisogno che sia il calcio a riempirmi: sono già pieno dello Spirito Santo", ha dichiarato.

L’ex giocatore di Barcellona, Juventus e Paris Saint-Germain ha raccontato anche il suo desiderio di conoscere sempre più profondamente Dio: "Sono uno che fa tante domande. Davanti a lui sono come un bambino. Gli chiedo tutto, voglio sapere sempre di più".

A colpire maggiormente sono state però le parole sul periodo trascorso in detenzione preventiva. Alves ha confrontato gli anni da calciatore professionista, caratterizzati da ingaggi milionari e trofei, con i 14 mesi vissuti nel carcere Brians 2 di Barcellona: "Guadagnavo milioni di euro, grazie a Dio e al calcio, ma in prigione, guadagnando 113 euro, ero più felice che quando prendevo milioni", ha raccontato.

L’ex terzino ha trascorso oltre un anno in carcere prima di ottenere la libertà provvisoria. Nel marzo 2025 il Tribunale Superiore di Giustizia della Catalogna ha annullato la precedente condanna a quattro anni e mezzo per un caso di aggressione sessuale. Oggi Alves porta avanti una nuova fase della sua vita attraverso testimonianze pubbliche incentrate sulla fede e sulla trasformazione personale, lontano dai riflettori del campo.

#2222. The four problems Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix at Man United: From big names causing unrest in the dressing room to an issue which plagued Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick before him, these are the items top of his Old Trafford in-tray

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.

With United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League standings, it’s clear why Pochettino has been brought in to replace Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the most pressing matters in Pochettino’s in-tray at Carrington as the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss and his backroom staff head for Manchester...

Mauricio Pochettino is the new manager of Manchester United - but the problems he has to fix are already piling up

It sounds obvious, but winning games to get United out of the Premier League drop zone has to be the first priority.

Everything at a football club flows from the results on the pitch, and United’s humiliating decline this season has had ramifications throughout Old Trafford and Carrington.

The players are clearly low on confidence which has only exacerbated the team’s dismal performances and brought just one win in 10 Premier League games, against newly-promoted Ipswich – United’s worst start in 40 years.

Diogo Dalot is a prime example, after fans cheered his substitution in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, and the defender cut a crestfallen figure as he left Old Trafford to go on international duty with Portugal.

The Stretford End also turned on the players as the atmosphere turned toxic after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth at the end of last month, having vented their anger towards the club’s ownership – the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at every opportunity.

That won’t go away anytime soon, but a winning team will at least take some of the sting out of the situation if appointing Pochettino can give United a ‘bounce’ and divert attention back onto the pitch.

United players are low on confidence, not least Diogo Dalot (left) whose substitution was cheered by his own fans against Aston Villa

The United team were also lambasted by the Stretford End after the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last month

Carrick enjoyed a good start, losing just two of his 17 games in charge in the second half of last season to earn a two-year contract, but United struggled under him this term due to a combination of poor recruitment, injuries and lack of fitness.

These are all issues that Pochettino must try to put right. There is little he can do about recruitment until the January transfer window opens and United have a chance to atone for their mistake in not signing cover at left back and centre forward last summer, which backfired spectacularly when both Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko picked up injuries.

He can, however, try to get more out of United’s £155million midfield signings Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again – Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and a United squad that was good enough to finish third in the Premier League last season.

Injuries have been a major problem with the hamstring strain that will keep Baleba out of action for Pochettino’s first few weeks in charge just the latest setback.

As well as Shaw, Sesko, Baleba and long-term casualty Manuel Ugarte, United have also lost Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui for parts of this season.

Pochettino must get more out of United’s £155million midfield signing Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again

United have struggled to keep up with their opponents since the opening day - a lack of fitness has plagued every manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer

The good news for Pochettino is that Shaw and Rashford are hoping to be fit for Anfield, while Matthijs de Ligt is available again after a year out with back problems. However, Sesko’s absence until the new year leaves the new boss without his most natural source of goals.

Fitness is another matter and United have looked short of it since the opening-day defeat at Hull City amid concerns that the coaching levels dropped off under Carrick and were too relaxed.

They covered 120.8 kilometres against Villa – the most in a league game under Carrick – and Pochettino will demand that and a whole lot more as he increases the work-rate among his new squad.

It’s a problem that has hindered a succession of United bosses going back to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and the Argentine must find a way to drill a better work ethic into United.

The problems at United this season have inevitably led to unrest in the dressing room, with the biggest issue centred around captain Bruno Fernandes.

News that Fernandes has rejected United’s latest contract offer has come as no surprise given his dramatic change in fortunes from last season, and Pochettino must find a way to get arguably United’s best player back in form and onside.

Having set a new Premier League record for assists and picked up a string of player of the year awards last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off a cliff as he struggled with an injury sustained at the World Cup, and he suffered the rare indignity of being benched for the loss to Bournemouth.

Never one to hide his mood very well, the 32-year-old criticised Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat by Como in what was a major blow to his head coach.

Never one to hide his mood very well, Bruno Fernandes has been disgruntled of late and rejected United's offer of a new contract

Lisandro Martinez looks to be headed for the exit door - although the arrival of his fellow Argentine Pochettino may help things

While the United hierarchy will try to persuade Fernandes to sign a new deal in keeping with their reduced wage structure and the fact he will turn 33 next year, Pochettino has to find a way of relighting the fire in his skipper.

Whether the club will make as much effort to keep Lisandro Martinez as he comes towards the end of his contract remains to be seen after another member of United’s leadership team took aim at Wilcox’s recruitment after the defeat by Atletico Madrid. It is said to have caused an angry clash between Martinez and summer signing Tielemans on the way back from Spain.

Martinez looks to be heading for the Old Trafford exit, but it will be interesting to see if the arrival of his compatriot Pochettino – a combative Argentine centre back in much the same mould as a player – has an impact on that.

As a former defender, Pochettino won’t need telling that leaking 15 goals in the last five games simply isn’t good enough. United have now let in 30 in all competitions this season, the most of any club in Europe’s top five leagues apart from Lens.

They have been appalling at the back, conceding in the opening seconds to Atletico, Como and Villa. Had they been able to hold out and prevent late equalisers against Everton and Tottenham, the additional four points would have them 12th in the table rather than in the relegation zone.

A revolving door of makeshift left backs in the absence of Shaw and Dorgu, De Ligt’s belated comeback and Martinez’s needless red card at Chelsea haven’t helped.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens, so composed last season, looks considerably more shaky behind a leaky and ever-changing back-four, and had arguably his worst game against Villa last weekend.

Pochettino couldn’t ask for a tougher first test than going to Anfield, and knows that United will have to start by being solid at the back.

#2221. Reina: «Rino non rallenterà». Lazio e Inter nella corsa scudetto

L’ex portiere considera evidente la forza dei nerazzurri e parla anche di Como, Roma, Milan, Juventus e Napoli.

Pepe Reina considera evidente la forza dell’Inter nella corsa scudetto, ma rassicura i tifosi della Lazio sull’impegno di Gattuso. Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, l’ex portiere dice: «Lo strapotere dell’Inter mi sembra evidente, per progetto e per forza degli interpreti. Posso rassicurare i laziali: Rino non rallenterà.»

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nel suo giudizio sul campionato c’è spazio anche per le altre squadre: «E il Como continuerà evolversi. Ma anche la Roma, con il calcio di Gasperini è una realtà. Milan e Juventus sono in una di quelle fasi che sembrano interlocutorie. Il Napoli è in difficoltà e mi dispiace. Ne verrà fuori, me lo auguro». Reina distingue così la forza dell’Inter dalla situazione delle altre formazioni citate.

Reina parla anche della classifica e dei due allenatori a cui è legato: «La Lazio è prima, il Como è quinto e su quelle panchine ci sono due miei amici che vedo e sento spesso. Gattuso mi ha segnato umanamente, però anche tatticamente ha proposte che mi hanno convinto.»

Il suo apprezzamento riguarda anche Fabregas: «Fabregas è un innovatore straordinario, che insegue metodi abbaglianti. Diventerà una guida per la categoria.» Sul paragone con Guardiola aggiunge: «Il Guardiola 3.0? Pep ha visto cose che altri non riuscivano a vedere, ha inventato, ha vinto e stravinto, ha conquistato. E Cesc lo ricorda».

#2219. Abate avvisa il Toro: "Il Napoli non ha i punti che meriterebbe. Allegri fortissimo nelle letture"

Mister Ignazio Abate, allenatore del Torino, è intervenuto in conferenza stampa in vista del big match col Napoli, invitando i suoi calciatori a non sottovalutare gli azzurri di Massimiliano Allegri nonostante le difficoltà di questa prima parte di stagione.

In carriera ha avuto Allegri... "Ho un rapporto speciale, ci lega uno scudetto: io ero giovane, mi fece migliorare nel nuovo ruolo. Mi porto dietro tanti insegnamenti, è un tecnico di alto livello e fortissimo nelle letture delle gare. Per noi sarà difficile, il Napoli non ha i punti che meriterebbe. Sarà uno stadio infuocato, serve personalità"

Come mai Allegri sta trovando così tante difficoltà a Napoli? Ed è stato lui a farle capire che avrebbe potuto diventare allenatore? "Non giudico una situazione di un'altra squadra, ho già difficoltà a pensare alla mia di situazione...(ride, ndr). Con Allegri ero molto giovane, avevo debuttato da terzino con Leonardo. I primi mesi non mi vedeva terzino ma centrocampista, poi verso fine settembre in un Milan-Real mi mise terzino e da lì iniziò la mia carriera. Nell'ultimo anno di carriera pensavo a un ruolo dirigenziale, mi scattò la scintilla quando feci il corso da allenatore"

Con Allegri ha parlato in questi mesi e in questi anni? "Lo incontro spesso, a Milano abitiamo nello stesso palazzo. E capita che scambiamo quattro chiacchiere"

Che soddisfazione sarebbe fare punti contro un maestro come Allegri? Anche Cairo ha parlato di un Toro che deve migliorare... "Non ci penso a dare un dispiacere a un mio ex allenatore. Mi auguro che i miei ragazzi riescano a togliersi una soddisfazione prendendo punti in uno stadio infuocato e perché ci darebbe ancora più convinzione, anche se mi baso sulla quotidianità e vedo le loro qualità ogni giorno".

In Spagna sono ricominciati i ritornelli sull'interesse del Barcellona per Alessandro Bastoni. Il Mundo Deportivo parla del mercato blaugrana e sostiene che il nerazzurro è nell'elenco dei terzini a cui il club blaugrana starebbe pensando: "Non si esclude la possibilità di ingaggiare un terzino qualora il mercato presentasse un'opportunità interessante.
