#2149. Family's fury as 'elite' athlete twin brothers are arrested by ICE while on their way to college in Alabama

Published: 20:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 21:42 EST, 14 November 2026

A dismayed mother and father spoke out after their 'elite' athlete twin sons were arrested by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) as they returned to their Alabama college.

Wallace State Community College soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, 19, were taken into ICE custody after a traffic stop on November 4 while on their way to campus, the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reported.

The Venezuelan twins were returning from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta, in Georgia when they were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer during a traffic stop in east-central Alabama.

The brothers graduated from Lawrenceville's Archer High School after a successful varsity soccer career that included a first ever region title for the school.

'This is the house of two elite soccer players,' Carlos Enrique Orta, their father, told the outlet.

Luis and Carlos are asylum seekers who applied for protections after legally entering the US on a tourist visa, like their parents.

That visa expired and the twins were granted US work permits and Georgia driver's licenses, according to the outlet.

A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), which oversees ICE, told the Daily Mail on Saturday that the brothers had legally entered the US with permission to stay on a temporary basis on June 21, 2022, but then 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws.'

Twin brothers and soccer players Luis and Carlos Orta Santoro, both 19, were taken into ICE custody on November 5 after being arrested the previous day

Luis and Carlos were region title-winning soccer players for Archer High School in Lawrenceville, Georgia

The brothers were arrested as they returned from visiting their parents, Carlos Enrique Orta and Reyna Santoro de Orta (both left)

The DHS spokesperson told the Daily Mail: 'All their claims will be heard by an immigration judge, and they will receive due process. This administration will not ignore the rule of law.'

'To be clear, pending applications do NOT confer legal status,' the statement continued.

Carlos was named the offensive player of the year and Luis the midfield player of the year by their high school this year.

They had received soccer scholarships to attend Wallace State, which they began doing this fall, but now face deportation to Venezuela.

'It's been hell,' Santoro de Orta, their mother, told the outlet.

She added that she supported ICE 'taking away the criminals' but said her children did not fit that description.

A final decision on the brothers' asylum case is still pending as they remain in custody.

The concerned mother claimed police said the twins' car had failed to come to a complete stop at a stop sign.

The brothers were arrested by a Lincoln Police Department officer as they were returning to Wallace State Community College, where they have soccer scholarships

The family applied for asylum protections after legally entering the country on a tourist visa. The DHS said the brothers 'illegally overstayed in defiance of our laws'

The Lincoln Police Department signed a partnership agreement with ICE in July.

ICE said the program allows trained local officers to exercise limited immigration authority during routine police work under federal supervision, according to the Cullman Tribune.

Luis and Carlos were booked into the Talladega County Jail on November 4 and transferred to ICE custody the following day.

Their father, Orta, described how the family was grappling with guilt as they shared what happened to their children.

'If anyone is at fault, it's me. It's us,' Orta told the outlet. 'Because I insist and I will continue to insist that Carlos and Luis came here because of a decision we made.'

He added: 'Carlos and Luis stayed here because of a decision from mom and dad. Carlos and Luis are here because of us.'

The Santoro twins were taken to the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana after their arrest, WABE reported.

The brothers have been taken to the the Pine Prairie ICE Processing Center in southern Louisiana

The Lincoln Police Department signed an partnership agreement with ICE in July. A department officer arrested the brothers

A friend of the twins, Nicolas Azcarate Florez, said he had spoken to them multiple times since they were taken into custody.

'They've been saying that they've been moved five times, so it has been difficult for them,' Azcarate Florez told the outlet.

Azcarate Florez said the brothers were 'players that you could just give the ball to, and you would know that they would do something good with it.'

'If we needed them, we would know that they would be there to help us out of a sticky situation,' he added.

The brothers were taken into custody on the same week that the Republican Party faced a historic blue wave in the midterm elections that was seen as a rebuke of the GOP's immigration policy.

One of President Donald Trump's first moves afterwards was to name Stephen Miller as the new White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles.

Miller, one of Trump's most loyal and longest-serving advisers going back to his first administration, is known for his hardline views on immigration.

Critics have cited Miller as the architect of some of Trump's most divisive policies, including separating migrant families during deportations in the President's first term.

#2148. Football slots explained: How the games work and what RTP really means

Bookmaker sponsorship has been part of English football for two decades, and the sport has also become one of the most common themes in online slot games.

Gambling sponsorship remains highly visible across the English Football League, despite recent changes at Premier League level.

Sponsored content. This article was produced in paid partnership with Slotozilla and contains sponsored links. 18+ only.

The shirts of clubs competing in each EFL division (Championship, League One and League Two) are virtually identical to those of the previous campaign, yet bookmakers’ logos have disappeared from the front of Premier League strips for the first time since the early 2000s owing to a voluntary agreement reached back in April 2023. That agreement does, however, only apply to the front of shirts specifically in the Premier League, and no equivalent restriction applies to EFL clubs.

The EFL has not sought to introduce any such restrictions and does not intend to, with the division remaining under the Sky Bet brand until 2029. Even in the Premier League, clubs are still able to acquire high-visibility sponsorships from bookmakers on shirt sleeves and LED boards throughout the stadium.

As such, the closeness between the two industries over the last 20 years has simultaneously given rise to a distinct genre within online gaming.

There are now dozens of slot games featuring stadiums, footballs, referees, penalties and trophies. Fans who want to compare titles or check RTP figures can use slot information sites as well as operators’ own pages.

For example, Slotozilla is a gambling-focused portal that has compiled thousands of slots along with technical information and free demo access. Such databases allow you to understand how a game works before you spend any money.

A football slot isn’t necessarily a complex, modern game with dozens of bonuses. Essentially, it’s a standard slot machine where football serves as a striking visual theme. Instead of cherries and sevens on the reels, you’ll see footballs, whistles and trophies, whilst bonus rounds have names such as ‘penalty’ or ‘free-kick’.

The majority of footballing slots are reliant on recognisable imagery, ranging from fan and player celebrations to trophies, penalty shoot-outs and stadium floodlights. Notable titles such as Football Rules! or Hugo Goal were created with the intention of recreating the vibrant atmosphere surrounding major tournaments instead of simulating real fixtures.

Playtech’s Football Rules!, released in 2007, is a good example of this early approach. It has five reels, 25 paylines, a bonus round and Wild and Scatter symbols, with a default RTP of 97.06 percent, according to Playtech. Here, football is purely a visual layer on top of standard slot mechanics.

Goal!!! by Booming Games shows how the genre has since moved on. Instead of five reels and three rows, it uses a 4x4 grid with 16 paylines running horizontally, vertically and diagonally. Booming Games lists its default RTP as 94.92 percent, with medium volatility.

The difference between these two games clearly illustrates that the only thing they have in common is the theme. The maths, RTP range and payout structure within the genre vary just as much as in any other category of slots.

A football slot does not replicate any real match or tournament, although they are sometimes released to coincide with specific sporting events.

One example is Play’n GO’s Hugo Goal, which was released two weeks before the start of the FIFA 2018 World Cup in Russia. Co-founder and CEO Johan Thörnqvist explained in the company’s press release that the company launched the game at the perfect moment to offer entertainment to players between matches along with providing cross-selling opportunities for partners.

The pattern repeats with every major tournament. Ahead of the World Cup in the US, Canada and Mexico in 2026, studios once again released football-themed titles to coincide with the event. Among them was Maradona Golden Goal from Blueprint Gaming, a sequel to the game licensed for the 2022 World Cup.

However, the tournament only influences the design and release timing, not what happens on the reels. Hugo Goal, with its penalty shoot-out series, feels very much in the spirit of football; however, every ‘save’ is determined by a random number generator, regardless of what happens on the actual pitch.

Every slot has an information screen that sets out its rules, paylines, bonus features and RTP. On UK-licensed sites, verified adult players can usually also view a demo version showing how those features work before any money is staked.

For example, Slotozilla, an online gaming review platform, offers demo versions that use a virtual balance. You can’t win real money there, but you can’t lose any either. Features such as Wilds, Scatters, free spins and payline or ways systems are all explained there. You don’t need to place a real bet at all to get to know a football slot.

Users often get confused about the RTP (Return to Player) statistic, which can be seen next to the name of every slot. This feature is usually misunderstood, however, and represents the theoretical percentage of funds that the game’s mathematical model returns to players over a very long period.

Essentially, an RTP of 97.06% in Football Rules! does not mean that a player will bet £100 and get £97.06 back. A single short session may end quite differently, and the RTP metric is instead meaningful as a long-term statistical indicator and as a way of comparing the mathematical models of different games.

Demo mode, however, only explains the game itself. As soon as a UK player moves on to real-money play, the terms and conditions attached to deposits and free spins are just as important as the RTP. Reading the full terms before accepting or activating any offer, including wagering requirements, avoids surprises later.

Football has transformed into a popular genre within slots, which is interesting in the wider context of gambling and its relationship with the sport. Exactly how much space a bookmakers’ sponsor should occupy on footballing shirts worn by the masses is often a divisive topic across the British footballing sphere, while slot developers have recreated the game's atmosphere without using any club's shirt.

But there is one fundamental difference between a match and a slot game. In football, nothing is known in advance - and that’s precisely why people watch it. In slots, on the other hand, everything is calculated in advance; the RTP, mechanics and terms are all laid out before the first spin, and you can view them for free.

If gambling is affecting you or someone close to you, free and confidential support is available 24/7 from the National Gambling Helpline on 0808 8020 133.

#2146. 5 Ian Evatt replacements Blackpool must consider ASAP

Blackpool have confirmed the sacking of Ian Evatt following a year in charge at Bloomfield Road, with the Tangerines now intent on reviving their fortunes under fresh management and avoiding a battle against relegation from League One.

Evatt had led the side to a respectable 13th-placed finish during the previous campaign after taking over from Steve Bruce, though the former Bolton Wanderers boss would struggle to get going once again at Bloomfield Road this term.

Last Saturday's 1-0 defeat away to fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon marked the sixth in just ten games for Blackpool, who now find themselves only positioned above Doncaster Rovers in 21st by virtue of goal difference at this moment in time.

Blackpool's key decision-makers eventually listened to intensified sack calls from supporters by relieving Evatt of his duties on Thursday afternoon, and whilst the relegation-threatened third-tier outfit have confirmed that Steve Thompson will be in charge for this weekend's clash with Wigan Athletic, the search for a replacement has already begun.

With that in mind, FLW has taken a close look at FIVE managers who Blackpool should be seriously considering as potential successors to Evatt.

One manager who should surely feature within Blackpool's thinking is Andy Woodman who, remarkably enough, currently finds himself out of work following a controversial EFL sacking for the ages from League One rivals Bromley.

Woodman had, of course, inspired the plucky Ravens' unprecedented rise into the EFL pyramid for the first time in their history before winning the League Two title against all odds last season, although matters both on and off the field in that particular corner of South London have not been plain-sailing as of late.

Nonetheless, it was a huge surprise when the 52-year-old's historic 289-match reign at Bromley came to an abrupt end last month, and one suspects he won't be sat around unattached for too long.

We rank all 24 League One stadiums by their ground's distance from the city or town, starting with the longest distance.

Woodman's resourceful ability to get the very best out of what was at his disposal with the Ravens certainly reads well, and he frequently elevated and identified talent with great success.

His strong body of work, albeit at a lower level, means that he should be entering the thinking of the Tangerines hierarchy in the coming days.

A previous specialist of the firefighting genre, Gary Rowett's knack in that field has faded in recent times and he may need to re-attempt his hand in a lower division.

As such, Rowett could represent the most outstanding realistic candidate available to Blackpool right now, with the former Derby County, Millwall and Stoke City boss having been linked with the vacancy at promotion hopefuls Bradford City prior to Michael Duff's appointment.

The last few years haven't reflected too kindly on Rowett, who led both Birmingham City and Leicester to relegations while setting Oxford United up for the same fate in the same season that he was in charge of the Foxes' demotion last time out.

Therefore, the wily 52-year-old may not score favourably in the consideration of Championship decision-makers and could instead drop to League One for the first time in his managerial career.

Previously, of course, Rowett has excelled in firing teams towards safety and, though much of his fresher work has been conducted on a short-term basis, there's no reason why he couldn't provide a stable, steady and longer-term presence with the Seasiders.

Matt Bloomfield, meanwhile, having reportedly held talks with Blackpool following the aforementioned Bruce's departure in October of last year, is only likely to re-emerge as a contender for the Tangerines' top job in the near future.

Bloomfield was ultimately unable to prevent Oxford's relegation to League One after succeeding Rowett, yet many believed his subsequent sacking from the Kassam Stadium to represent a surprise and even harsh call - albeit Aaron Ramsey has since vindicated the Yellows' change in direction.

Still aged just 42, Bloomfield's stock has taken a few hits and he's perhaps yet to recover from an ill-fated spell in charge of Luton Town, in which he fell narrowly short of ensuring survival on the 2024/25 second-tier term's final-day before failing to inspire a tangible promotion push in League One.

He has, however, previously excelled at this level, with Wycombe Wanderers having been situated just two points behind eventual-runaway champions Birmingham at the time of his departure to Luton in January 2025.

Bloomfield may now require a sustained spell back in League One leading a side with more modest expectations such as the Chairboys, where he was able to work his magic - and Blackpool can provide just that.

In contrast to Rowett and Bloomfield, Stuart Maynard lacks pedigree above League Two level, but that shouldn't rule the ex-Notts County and York City boss out of contention.

Indeed, at the age of 46 and with an obvious appetite to prove his managerial mettle higher up the pyramid, Maynard could be an ideal candidate for Blackpool in their efforts to not only survive, but begin laying the foundational blueprint for longer-term stability and success.

Much like Woodman at Bromley, Maynard's dismissal from York in the wake of promotion back to League Two following a decade-long exile as National League champions with no fewer than 108 points was scarcely believable. The difference, of course, is that Maynard did not even receive the opportunity to lead the Ministermen into the current campaign, and their loss could turn out to be Blackpool's gain.

Maynard has a solid body of work to boast of from his time at Notts County, where he failed to deliver promotion but did take the Magpies into the fourth-tier play-offs during their second season back at the level and ultimately put the foundations in place for Martin Paterson to go one better with the Meadow Lane outfit.

Blackpool fans, having sat through an overly-patient and slow-paced possession-based style under Evatt, would likely warm to a more dynamic, attack-oriented approach through Maynard, who would tick many boxes for the League One strugglers.

A more left-field option with greater risk but no shortage of potential upside, Ryan Mason remains available following his departure from West Bromwich Albion at the start of the year and represents an interesting candidates for lower-ranked EFL outfits to consider.

Mason was highly-thought-of during his time coaching Tottenham Hotspur and even taking occasional interim charge of the Lilywhites, which meant that many were surprised when the one-cap ex-England international failed to get going at West Brom.

He would take just nine wins from 27 matches across all competitions with the Baggies before being dismissed ahead of a relegation battle in the deeper stages of the previous campaign, with James Morrison going on to prove just how much his two predecessors in Mason and Eric Ramsey had underperformed at the Hawthorns.

It was, however, Mason's first senior, full-time gig, and it would be harsh to judge him entirely from that alone.

Blackpool fans, was it the right time to sack Ian Evatt? Who would be your number-one replacement choice, and what do you make of FLW's selections? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

Mason showed plenty of signs at West Brom that suggest he'd be a more-than-capable candidate somewhat lower down the ladder, with his progressive style, experience with young talent and connections within the game all representing healthy selling points for a club in Blackpool's position.

It's essentially a case of risk versus reward, and only Blackpool's key boardroom figures can decide whether it's a gamble worth taking amid the threat of relegation to League Two.

They do have a history of appointing older managers with their best years very much in the past, though, and there are worse options than going for a change of tact and rolling the dice on Mason.

#2145. On The Road: Overpowered by County, but Accies are making small steps in the long road back from the abyss

Published: 08:28 EST, 15 November 2026 | Updated: 10:25 EST, 15 November 2026

The depth of the descent of Hamilton Accies and Ross County would make it understandable if tickets for a fixture between the two carried warning about the bends when leaving New Douglas Park.

The decompression sickness caused by emerging from a League One fixture for two sides who should be much higher must be severe. There may, however, be a positive prognosis.

Accies, despite their defeat, are whispering about stability, even though ‘legacy debt’ has to be faced, perhaps contested.

County, meanwhile, will not say it even in a whisper but Saturday’s victory takes them eight points clear at the top and heavily fancied for the title. The Staggies have one set of hooves in the Championship.

Scottish football, of course, does not restrict itself to the cliched fare of top of the table clashes so New Douglas Park hosted a striker who is 39 later this month, a winger who was once a Scottish international, and a gentleman in the stands who once played against George Best. And a Ross County fan who regularly travels up from North Wales.

These exotic avenues demand to be explored but perennial questions about the financial health of the Accies had to be asked, too, after reports this week stating that hospitality packages at the club were being suspended.

An Accies fan feels the pain of defeat during Saturday's home loss to Ross County

Allan Currie, chairman, answered them over a half-time pie.

‘We have come on in leaps and bounds but every week seems to throw up different challenges,’ he said. ‘We have a level of debt that we have inherited and we are working with the creditors to try to navigate our way through that.’

Matters on the field are positive, despite Saturday’s defeat.

‘The guys on the pitch, manager, and his staff have been unbelievable. Surviving in this league last season was phenomenal given what they were going through but it couldn’t be better now,’ he said. ‘Off the pitch, we are fighting with the different challenges we have. We are in a much better place even if we are not out the woods yet.’

Asked what the level of pressure on him, he said: ‘I am the guy on the ground but Rob Edwards is carrying out negotiations.’

Edwards, through his Morley Group, took over the club earlier this year but has been sideswiped by a number of claims for payment. However, Currie has faith in the owner.

‘Without him, the club would not survive. Rob should take all the credit,’ he said.

Asked what the short-term aims for the club were, Currie replied with a smile: ‘A goal in the second half would be good.’ A goal was scored but not for the Accies.

But the club remain in second place and the play-offs seem a more than reasonable prospect.

Ross County goalscorer Kieran Phillips battles with Hamilton's Kai Smutek

With 10 minutes to go, Hamilton brought on their latest signing. Barrie McKay, who has played for Scotland and scored for Rangers in a Scottish Cup semi-final against Celtic. His considerable achievements, though, paled in comparison to the subject of a casual conversation in the bar before the match.

‘I played against George Best,’ said Alan McDougall, with an air so off-hand one could have believed he was merely ordering another pint.

‘Yes, I played 200 games for the Accies. Davie McParland brought me here as a 21-year-old and I played for about six years. I went to Stranraer for a year and then went down south. I played against Best with the Accies.’

The Northern Irish genius played for Hibernian in 1979-80. ‘He was well past his best and that was sad,’ said McDougall. Best’s addiction to alcohol had taken a severe toll.

‘I came back to watch games five or six years ago,’ said McDougall. ‘When the club went to Clyde, it destroyed me. What is fantastic is that the people that are now in control seem to be turning it around.’

There was a mood of cautious optimism from other fans. ‘I have been a fan since forever, well the 1980s at least,’ said Gavin Fullarton. ‘I have seen this team in every division. I have seen them in the downs and downs. But I think we are going in the right direction. So far.’

He added: ‘The new guys seem to know what they are doing. They are communicative.’

There were 1,216 fans in the ground on Saturday with 300 stalwarts travelling down from the north. Colin Richardson, an Accies supporter, was asked why so many had stuck by the club.

‘It’s about loyalty,’ he said. ‘You can’t pick and choose when you support your team. At the moment it is all about small steps. It has to be about stability.’

A Ross County fan had travelled up from North Wales. The journey to Scotland is a familiar one for Ian Ellson. ‘I have been all over Scotland to watch Ross County,’ he said. ‘Twenty years ago I visited Ross County and I was spoiled rotten. I decided to follow them.’

A social worker, he averages one visit a month. ‘I live and breathe Ross County,’ he said. ‘This season we are going up.’

Welsh Staggies fan Ian Elson and Englishman Ray Griffiths travelled far for Saturday's game

Brian Graham would not be so bullish. He is 39 this month and has learned enough about football to know that predictions are made only to make the speaker seem foolish down the line.

He was, though, expansive about what is happening at County. He joined the club for the second time in the summer after Stuart Kettlewell, the manager, convinced him of the ambitions in Dingwall.

‘This is a club where I have had success before so I know how good a club it can be,’ he said. ‘It’s not been great for a couple of seasons but in the summer the manager set out his stall very early. It was about leaving egos at the door, building a togetherness and having a change of culture at the club. I think you are seeing that now.’

The early signs were good for the striker who dropped down from Falkirk in the Premiership to play in Dingwall.

‘We had good pre-season performances against Aberdeen and Dundee and that was a solid building block,’ he said.

Brian Graham celebrates after scoring his 21st goal of the season for County

Graham converted a first-half penalty to reach a tally of 21 goals this season and the Christmas trees are not up yet. ‘I get a lot of plaudits for scoring goals but others in the team are scoring a lot too,’ he said. ‘We are scoring team goals.’

Has he set a target for the season? ‘When I came back I knew I had to score 13 to reach 50 goals for the club in two spells,’ he said. ‘I always set down targets in a wee black book but now I might need to readjust that.’

It was a night of adjustment for Darian MacKinnon. He had set a victory target but was condemned to accept defeat. He would not concede the league race was over. ‘We have to play them twice,’ he said.

He added ‘We are going in the right direction. The owners have put money in and they have backed us.’

Asked to pinpoint a factor that has contributed to the team sitting second, he said: ‘The most positive thing for me this season is that this is now a good place to come into your work after the last three or four seasons. We are all actually enjoying coming to our work.’

There is work to be done on and off the pitch but the Accies are surviving. And that is the biggest result.

#2143. Viktor Gyökeres makes Arsenal future clear as striker responds to exit speculation

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Viktor Gyökeres has put to bed any doubts over his future at Arsenal by stating his desire to stay.

The striker has been under question over his long-term future under Mikel Arteta after a difficult start to the 2026/27 season. His latest comments suggest he will not be seeking a move away from north London.

Gyökeres moved to Arsenal for £63.5m from Sporting Lisbon last summer. He’s played a key role in the club winning the Premier League last season with 14 league goals.

However, he has not featured as much this season. Kai Havertz often being Arteta’s go-to man centrally, resulting in him only starting once in the Premier League.

This has led to some speculation that the Sweden international may look at his options in January. However, his latest interview with the Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen suggests otherwise.

Gyökeres was asked if he wants to stay at Arsenal and has made it clear he wants to continue his career at the Emirates.

The striker also spoke about his relationship with Arteta.

He explained that they regularly discuss football, the team’s approach and the opposition. Those conversations also help him understand what Arteta expects when he is selected to start.

It is a key point to note that just because he hasn’t had much time on the pitch doesn’t mean there have been any issues between the two.

Gyökeres has begun to show his worth again in recent weeks. He found the net against Fleetwood in the League Cup and then Slavia Prague in the Champions League.

This came after a long time to get his first goal of the season and gives him the chance to remind Arteta what he can bring to the team.

There is no doubt that Gyökeres has not lived up to the expectations he had when he came from Portugal.

But his overall effect cannot be ignored. He has contributed 23 goals and 6 assists in 69 games for Arsenal.

The challenge will be finding a way to get the best out of him and Havertz. They add different attributes, and Arteta will have plenty of options to choose from depending on the opposition.

They will also want to avoid losing someone they have invested heavily in so early on. Gyökeres has a contract until 2030, so they are in a great position.

His latest comments will help to reassure fans that he is not looking to leave the club after stating his ambition to play more games and make himself an indispensable part of Arteta’s squad.

The main thing for Arsenal will be to make sure that he can turn this attitude into consistent performances. Gyökeres has made his intentions clear and now needs to show why they brought him to North London in the first place.

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United travel to Italy on Wednesday, looking for their first win since September 10, when they face Como in the Champions League.

Michael Carrick’s side have struggled to build any momentum this season. Sunday’s 1-1 draw against Leeds extended their winless run to six matches in all competitions, leaving United with just seven points from their opening seven Premier League games.

The pressure on Carrick continues to grow. A win in Europe would offer some relief, but Como will not make life easy for Manchester United.

Manchester United began their Champions League campaign with a convincing 4-0 win over Sabah FK but lost 2-0 to Atletico Madrid in their next match. They have since drawn with Leeds, having also failed to beat Fulham and Tottenham in the Premier League.

Their last six matches across all competitions have produced three draws and three defeats. Michael Carrick is in pressure of his own and needs a response from his players, particularly with United sitting 13th in the Premier League and 13th in the Champions League standings.

Como have shown more promise. Cesc Fabregas’ side beat RB Leipzig 4-1 in Europe before losing 3-2 to Feyenoord. They returned to winning ways against Fiorentina, claiming a 3-1 victory that moved them up to fifth in Serie A, with 14 points from seven games.

Como have scored 11 goals and conceded eight across their last six matches in all competitions. United have struggled, with their only clean sheet of the season coming against Sabah FK.

United have several confirmed absentees ahead of the trip to Italy. Patrick Dorgu, Manuel Ugarte and Benjamin Sesko are ruled out, while Leny Yoro is suspended for the European fixture after picking a red against Atletico Madrid.

Como will be without Assane Diao, who is sidelined with a thigh injury. Moise Kean has a shin problem and is a doubt, while Trevoh Chalobah is also a fitness concern with a muscular issue.

The match takes place at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday, October 21, with kick-off at 5:45 pm BST.

UK viewers can watch the Champions League fixture live on TNT Sports 2 and HBO Max.

Rio Ferdinand has admitted he is disappointed that Manchester United failed to sign Ayyoub Bouaddi, with the highly-rated midfielder now making an impression at Manchester City.

Manchester City beat several rivals to secure Bouaddi’s signature over the summer in a deal worth £86 million. The Morocco international became the Premier League’s most expensive teenager, and Rio Ferdinand believes Manchester United missed out on a special talent.

The former United defender was particularly impressed by Bouaddi’s second-half cameo during City’s Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain last week. Ferdinand was left frustrated by what he saw from the teenager, who turned 19 this month.

“Just that little cameo against PSG makes you go, ‘oh, I can’t believe we missed out on that. I can’t believe it.’ I’m so gutted, so gutted. He’s bad! He’s so calm under pressure.”

#2140. 3 reasons why Bristol Rovers must sack Steve Evans

It was just a few short months ago that optimism was high and Bristol Rovers were widely being tipped for a hugely successful season. The Gas had ended the 2025-26 season unbeaten in nine matches and then started the new campaign by breaking the club record for consecutive wins at home. The optimism appeared well-placed.

Steve Evans was being lauded by Gasheads who were daring to dream. Iconic scenes of the gaffer in the Thatchers will be hard to replicate.

Now we’re approaching the festive period, and Gasheads are up in arms with large portions of the fanbase calling for Evans to go.

The Gas are once more on a miserable run of defeats in the league and have a manager either by accident or by nature creating division between himself and supporters, and even perhaps himself and his players.

Supporters have become increasingly frustrated by the manager's post-match comments in recent times, adding to the dismay at results on the pitch.

With so many Gasheads now calling for Evans to go, Football League World offers three reasons why now is the right time to act.

The last time Bristol Rovers were on such a deep losing streak — a run that saw the Gas fall to a club record 10 straight league defeats — the ownership decided to act and dismissed Darrell Clarke. A man widely seen as a great of the club following his promotion success years earlier. Rovers' latest defeat under Evans, going down 2-0 at home to Chesterfield, was their eighth loss in their last 10 matches in League Two.

When you compare the final 12 League matches for Darrell Clarke (one win, one draw, 10 losses) with Steve Evans' last 12 league matches to-date (two wins, one draw and nine losses), there is very little between them.

Both men, though, can have strong claims to be deserving of more time to put things right at the club.

Darrell Clarke was, and remains, a hero for Gasheads. Clarke is one of Bristol Rovers' most successful managers in history, having achieved a unique feat by gaining back-to-back promotions. And his connection with the fan base is unrivaled by any manager, perhaps since Paul Trollope.

Steve Evans has won nine promotions across his 32 years in management. And was able to turn the Pirates' fortunes around following his arrival after Clarke's dismissal last season, enjoying a run of eight straight league victories (their best run since the 1950’s) alongside breaking the club record for consecutive home wins. All of which means he may have plenty of credit in the bank with the current Rovers ownership, even if support among fans has all but extinguished.

As pressure increases on Bristol Rovers manager Steve Evans, we looked at six potential replacements the Gas should consider.

Evans caused a stir earlier this week when his post-Chesterfield comments left supporters confused and even concerned.

Following the Pirates’ defeat to Chesterfield, Evans took to the media to unleash a barrage of comments that left many Gasheads asking what on earth he was on about, and ultimately forced Evans into the most remarkable backtrack.

On Saturday, Evans told the media that he and his staff were being let down by “inconsistent and poor players”. Players, incidentally, who were predominantly recruited by Evans and his staff. Whilst perhaps unhelpful to the cause of pulling your squad together, these comments were not what got the heckles up amongst Rovers supporters. Instead, it was his remarks that many interpreted to be an allegation against a previous manager having been turning up to work at Bristol Rovers drunk when results were going against them.

Evans told local media after the match on Saturday: "We’re not doing our jobs, but we’re being let down by inconsistent players. Poor players, in my opinion."

He then went on to add: "I’m still first in. Half six, till six. I’m watching games midweek. I’m not like before, when they’re coming in at nine o’clock, leaving at two, being drunk half the week. That’s not me, yeah."

It sparked widespread condemnation of Evans and also speculation as to who he was referring to.

On Monday, Steve Evans was forced into an incredible backtrack from those comments as he spoke to Bristol Live in an attempt to quash the speculation. The under-pressure veteran manager told the local news outlet: "I get really annoyed when people speculate or make something up when I speak openly. I spoke about other managers waiting for payoffs, and yes, that happens in football because our jobs are hard to get, and you can be out of work for some time."

Adding: "Further, I spoke about some individuals having alcohol-related issues here. Some have made two plus two = 12, with social media alluding to I was referring to one particular manager, and nothing could be further from the truth. I was actually generalising about the behaviour of some managers when pressure mounts. I am indeed the opposite. Work and Bristol Rovers are what matter to me. I need a clear focus. However, that cannot be attributed to many other individuals."

Football League World has also spoken directly to players who were at Bristol Rovers during previous regimes, who strongly denied suggestions that any manager turned up drunk while they were playing at the club.

For a large swathe of supporters who were undecided whether Evans was the right man to guide the Gas out of their latest slump, this episode has tipped the scales.

In recent seasons, Bristol Rovers have acted in the weeks leading up to Christmas with four managerial changes happening in mid-December since 2018. And with the transfer market opening on January 1st, along with question marks around the strength of the squad Steve Evans has assembled, there's an argument for making that decision sooner.

Any prospective new manager will need matches and plenty of time on the training ground to assess the quality of this Bristol Rovers squad before setting in motion any recruitment plans. A new manager will need to identify the weak spots in the squad, starting perhaps with bringing in sufficient goalkeeper backup, and trying to address the lack of potency in the Gas attack.

Rovers have six matches scheduled for December, including a busy festive period. And with the Gas currently looking in the wrong direction on the League Two table, the pressure will be on any new manager from the outset.

#2139. Jussi Jääskeläinen praises Arsenal star David Raya

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Former Premier League goalkeeper Jussi Jääskeläinen thinks David Raya is the best goalkeeper in the division right now.

But the former Bolton Wanderers star feels the Arsenal No.1 has more to prove before he can be put up with the all-time greats of the competition.

Jääskeläinen recently spoke to Kasinopartio.com, where he praised Raya’s performances and the understanding he has developed with Arsenal’s defenders.

“Raya has been a fantastic signing. He has a great relationship with the centre-backs; even when the back four changes, everything works well.”

The Spaniard has played a key role for Mikel Arteta since his arrival from Brentford. His organisation of the backline, key saves and contribution to Arsenal’s build up play have helped him to be a standout player.

In 2012, Raya began his journey in English football when he moved to Blackburn Rovers from Spain. At that time, he was just a young teenager unfamiliar with English football.

His short spell at Southport introduced him to senior football. Soon, he returned to Blackburn and forged a career ahead of moving to Brentford in 2019. After four years with Brentford, Raya achieved success at the club, helping them to the Premier League.

The player’s performances in the higher leagues caught the attention of Arsenal, and Arteta signed him on loan to the Emirates in 2023 before making the move permanent the following summer.

It didn’t take long for Raya to establish himself in the team. He took home the Premier League Golden Glove, having achieved 16 clean sheets in 32 appearances.

This was a significant milestone in his first season with the Arsenal team, and he has since remained as number one, playing a key role in the club’s pursuit of titles.

While Jääskeläinen said Raya is the best goalkeeper in the Premier League at the moment, he does not think he should be up there with the most experienced.

He believes other goalkeepers have earned an advantage through their consistency over a longer period.

“You have lots of top goalkeepers that I think are still a little bit ahead because of the years they’ve done it in the Premier League.”

“He’s not up there with them yet, but he’s definitely going in the right direction.”

Raya has already proven he can play to the top standard. However, it will be his consistency moving forward that will define his long-term reputation.

Petr Čech, Peter Schmeichel and Edwin van der Sar have all gained great reputations over the years. There is still plenty of time for Raya to do the same, but he will need to keep up his high standards whilst wearing an Arsenal shirt.

At just 31, Raya has a lot left in his career. If he can continue playing at this level, it will make the debate around whether he is one of the best goalkeepers in the Premier League even more intriguing.

#2138. Michael Carrick handed lifeline ahead of Chelsea trip

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Michael Carrick has come under immense pressure as a disjointed Manchester United sit just two places above the relegation places.

Despite the scrutiny and the news of a possible sacking, Michael Carrick has been given another chance at Manchester United.

Michael Carrick will remain in charge of Manchester United for their Premier League trip to Chelsea on Saturday after the club decided to give their under-pressure head coach another opportunity to turn things around.

United have gone eight games without a win in all competitions, with Sunday’s humiliating 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth leaving them 16th in the Premier League table, just one point above the relegation zone.

Carrick’s position looked increasingly uncertain after the Bournemouth loss. As a result, United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox were at Carrington on Monday to discuss the situation.

It has been reported by Sky Sports that United have considered other options internally as well to replace Micahel Carrick but for the weekend, they are sticking with Michael Carrick.

Carrick took training on Tuesday and the decision means he has at least one more match to convince the club’s hierarchy that he can get United back on track.

Gary Neville admitted he was surprised that Carrick had survived the immediate threat of losing his job, although he welcomed the decision.

“I am surprised, but I am happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,” Neville said in Sky Sports.

The former United captain explained that Carrick’s actions after the Bournemouth defeat had made him think the manager was preparing to say goodbye to the supporters.

“It looked like he was walking round at the end on his own with the players behind him, like it was almost a goodbye lap,” Neville added.

Fans continued singing the manager’s name after the final whistle, while the rest of the team drew boos.

Despite his surprise, Gary Neville hopes Micahel Carrick can use the extra time to get a response from his squad.

“I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him in the last few weeks,” he said.

The trip to Chelsea now becomes a crucial test for Micahel Carrick but United need a result and a far better performance to ease the pressure at Old Trafford.

#2136. Barnsley have a far bigger problem than Daniel Stendel right now

Daniel Stendel was the returning hero in the summer when he arrived back at Barnsley for a second spell as manager.

However, it has been anything but a success, with the club sitting in the relegation zone and in the midst of a long winless run.

The Reds are only above bottom-side Bromley, who have parted company with their manager, Andy Woodman, on goal difference. They have just two wins to their name, with three draws, and eight losses from their opening 13 matches of the league campaign.

Burton Albion, who shipped six in one match against Milton Keynes Dons, and Bromley, who saw Sheffield Wednesday score seven against them, are the only League One teams with worse defensive records than Stendel’s men.

At the other end of the pitch, it is no better. Barnsley have scored just 13 goals, with fellow relegation-zone side Peterborough United, AFC Wimbledon, and outliers Bradford City the only sides to have scored less.

Barnsley have claimed just two of the last 27 points available to them, and despite thumping wins against lower division sides in the FA Cup and EFL Trophy, have not won in league action since early September.

The statistics do not make for better reading either. The Tykes are 18th for xG conceded and have underperformed their xG created by more than five goals, according to FotMob.

The overall xG table places Barnsley 19th, four places higher than their current position, but that is still far below the hopes and aspirations of the Reds’ faithful.

Stendel was a promotion winning manager in his first stint at Oakwell, before the fickle nature of football reared its ugly head and the board sacked him following a winless run.

The German has enjoyed limited success since his 2019 departure, at Hearts in Scotland and Nancy in France, before returning to Hannover 96 to coach their reserve team.

Daniel Stendel's first vs second Barnsley spell (source: Transfermarkt)

The fixture list shows no mercy either, with Stendel having to prepare his side for a South Yorkshire derby against Dave Challinor and his Owls, before a trip to imperious Bradford City just days later.

The obvious answer might be to sack Stendel, after a nine-game winless run in League One.

But, that would only make the German a scapegoat for much deeper and more troubling problems. Barnsley have underinvested for years and failed to replace their departed stars.

A suitable replacement for Davis Keillor-Dunn, who is now at Wednesday on loan from Wrexham, was never sought, nor was it for David McGoldrick after his exit from the club more recently. Adam Phillips left in the summer for a fellow third tier side, with Cameron McGeehan adding a strong midfield option without adequately and directly replacing the skills that Phillips brought to the table.

Daniel Stendel is already under pressure at Barnsley after returning to the club in the summer

The Barnsley squad has seen repeated underinvestment by a board that has lost touch and damaged almost beyond repair its connection to the fanbase at the heart of the Tykes.

Removing Stendel and adding another name to the revolving door of head coaches and manager might be the easiest option, but it is far from being the solution to the gaping holes that have grown and been allowed to fester under sub-par direction.

#2135. Sonia Bompastor's side show their teeth as Chelsea sink the reigning champions to reclaim top spot in WSL title race: Chelsea 1-0 Man City

By SAMARA WATTS and TARA ANSON-WALSH, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 10:42 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 11:33 EST, 15 November 2026

Chelsea secured a deserved 1-0 victory over Manchester City at Stamford Bridge to leapfrog their rivals and reclaim top spot in the WSL table.

Sandy Baltimore's first-half goal was enough to ensure Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blow the title race wide open.

After keeping the reigning WSL champions at bay following an early barrage, Chelsea grew in confidence but still lacked the cutting edge that had seen them held to back-to-back draws in the past week.

A moment of magic from Baltimore in the fourth minute of stoppage time ensured history would not repeat itself.

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson, a move which appeared to invigorate the visitors, but Chelsea held firm to pick up all three points.

Daily Mail Sport's Tara Anson-Walsh and Samara Watts were at Stamford Bridge to bring you the things we learned...

Chelsea inflicted City's first defeat of the season and blew the title race wide open

City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita was sent off in the 75th minute for a rash challenge on Alyssa Thompson

Devastation for Kadeisha Buchanan, who was hooked after 11 minutes by Bompastor. The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match as she looked out of her depth against Bunny Shaw, ever a precarious place to be against the league’s top striker.

Buchanan gave an early ball away to allow Shaw to race through towards the Chelsea goal, and a few minutes later was again outmuscled and outpaced by the Jamaican striker, although City failed to capitalise on both occasions.

The 31-year-old Canada international looked devastated when her number flashed up on the board after just 12 minutes and reluctantly welcomed a hug from her manager as she headed straight for the tunnel.

Her replacement, the 20-year-old Veerle Buurman, who was outstanding against Shaw in the two sides’ last meeting in the FA Cup last season, changed the game, giving Chelsea a more solid platform to build upon as they grew in confidence.

Bompastor shut down suggestions that the move had been ruthlessly tactical at full time, saying that Buchanan had picked up a head injury during training on Friday.

'She was fine after the training session, she was fine in the evening and we assessed her again this morning and everything was fine,' Bompastor said.

'I had this information on what happened yesterday and I just felt, watching her from the beginning of the game, she was not herself. I took the responsibility to make this substitution. I was almost forced to do that because, I know my player, and I know she was not right in the game.'

For those sceptical, it certainly improved things.

The centre back has been one of Chelsea’s standout performers this season but had an unusually shaky start to this match and was hooked after just 11 minutes

Women’s football royalty Sarina Wiegman and Emma Hayes braved the chilly climes of Stamford Bridge to witness the showdown between the WSL heavyweights on Saturday afternoon.

The freshly anointed honorary Dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes and the pair chatted warmly, with Wiegman laughing as Hayes attempted to encourage her to celebrate Chelsea's victory at full time. This is a relationship that will no doubt drop in cordiality as the sand in the hourglass ahead of next summer’s World Cup continues to run down.

Wiegman had several England players on her watching brief, not least young Lexi Potter, whose stock has risen dramatically this season. The 20-year-old put in another assured performance against the reigning champions, continuing to demonstrate her maturity in the highest stakes, which will no doubt put her in a good position ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement.

Elsewhere, the Dutch coach will have been alarmed by the number of crunching tackles put in against her right back, Lucy Bronze, in this match. If there is one player that she will want to wrap up in cotton wool ahead of Brazil, it is the recently turned 35-year-old Bronze for her steadfast leadership and relentless athleticism.

One player looking to make an impact ahead of Tuesday’s squad announcement was Aggie Beever-Jones, who has struggled this season and was left out of Sonia Bompastor’s starting line-up. An injury to Melvine Malard saw Beever-Jones gain more minutes than she would have expected, but it felt like another afternoon of deja vu for the 23-year-old forward as she failed to convert a number of chances despite finding herself in good positions.

Meanwhile, in Manchester, Ella Toone's hopes of forcing her way back into Sarina Wiegman's plans suffered another blow as the 27-year-old was once again left out of Eva Olid's starting line-up for United's 2-0 win over Crystal Palace. Toone watched on as fellow Lioness Maya Le Tissier opened the scoring with a superb long-range strike, and the two-time European champion will no doubt be growing increasingly concerned as Brazil draws closer.

The freshly anointed honorary dame Wiegman sat next to Hayes at the WSL showpiece at Stamford Bridge and the pair chatted warmly

Melvine Malard’s absence raises questions about who Chelsea’s main goalscorer will be this season. The squad has lacked a clinical edge without England striker Lauren James, who is out with a hamstring injury until the international break.

The French forward went off injured after 35 minutes with a suspected hamstring injury. Although she missed Chelsea’s opening games after picking up a knock in pre-season, she has been the Blues’ top scorer in the absence of Lauren James with six league goals so far.

Chelsea are averaging 24 shots per game, an unprecedented rate across a WSL campaign, but have recently struggled to convert their chances. They were held to a 0-0 draw against BK Hacken midweek in the UWCL and a 1-1 draw against Everton last weekend.

Malard leaving the pitch meant Chelsea struggled to find a creative spark up front. Her replacement Aggie Beever-Jones has been dealing with an ankle injury, and is still trying to find her feet with only one goal in the WSL.

Head coach Bompastor said: ‘The frustration sometimes comes from us not being ruthless and clinical.’

A moment of magic from Malard’s French international teammate Sandy Baltimore was enough to make it 1-0 just before half time with the team’s first shot on target. However, Baltimore was substituted at half time to manage her minutes, and Chelsea were unable to capitalize on any of their chances in the second half.

Bompastor said: ‘From the outside it seems like we have had a lot of injuries, but we have been playing every three days.’

‘I knew coming into the game we were not as fresh as we would like to be, but that’s our environment.

‘We want to play in every competition but the players are not robots,’

Melvine Malard’s injury could cause more problems for the Blues’ attack, as they registered just two shots on target today and scraped the three points.

Malard limped off in the first half and meant Chelsea struggled for a creative spark up front

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box and took down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal in the 75th minute.

The Blues were mounting a rapid attack down the left hand side, with Thompson just outside the box when Yamashita missed the ball and brought her to the ground.

The Japanese goalkeeper was shown a straight red card and was sent off the pitch. This was City’s first red card in the WSL since November 2023, and a rare moment of madness from the usually-composed 31-year-old.

The referee allowed City three minutes to replace the Japanese goalkeeper, with Scotland’s number one Eartha Cumings coming on to replace forward Aoba Fujino.

Her first test arrived only a minute later, as Aggie Beever-Jones' right-footed shot from the resulting indirect free kick dropped dangerously, but she was saved by the crossbar.

The bigger question now is whether Yamashita's absence - which could amass to three games - will have a lasting impact on their title race.

In the short-term against Chelsea, City reacted well. Andree Jeglertz said at full time: ‘The players dealt with it in a good way, so even though we were one player down we had a couple of great opportunities to score a goal. Of course it affected the game but that is not why we lost.’

Stamford Bridge was in uproar as Manchester City goalkeeper Ayaka Yamashita rushed out of her box to take down Alyssa Thompson, who had a clear chance on goal

Chelsea’s win at the Bridge blows the title race wide open, as they are now just one point ahead of City at the top of the WSL table.

Bompastor’s side ended City’s unbeaten streak, and they now have 24 league goals compared to City’s 16 after 10 games.

However, with seven shots and just one on target this game, Chelsea will need to look at their attacking options as they take on Liverpool and London City Lionesses before the international break.

Bompastor said: ‘It’s a nice feeling to be top of the table right now and to win against these top sides, but I know we still have a lot of work to be done and it’s early on in the season so many things can happen.’

City were unable to create opportunities in front of goal, with the WSL’s all-time leading goalscorer Vivianne Miedema’s return overshadowed by Ayaka Yamashita’s nightmare in goal.

City head coach Andree Jeglertz said: ‘They managed to score on their big chance and (it was a) great finish.

'We also had some great opportunities where we didn’t manage to score, but I think we deserve more than going away from here with no points.’

London City Lionesses face Arsenal tomorrow at the Emirates, and a win in north London could bring them four points behind the new WSL leaders, and really start to make things interesting.

#2134. Mikel Merino speaks out on Arsenal role as January rumours grow

Lucie Turner writes about Arsenal for Read Arsenal and Newcastle United for Read Newcastle. A long-time Arsenal supporter, she also follows rugby, snooker, darts and Formula 1. Her work covers match previews and reports, breaking news, player profiles and opinion pieces.

Merino has played down any speculation around his potential exit during January. He has made it clear he will fight to keep his place in the squad.

He also spoke about speculation around Martin Zubimendi, who has been linked with Atletico Madrid.

Both players have been questioned over their role in Mikel Arteta’s midfield. There is increasing competition for positions at the Emirates.

Merino feels that there is always an intense fight for places in top-level football. He spoke about how strong and deep Arsenal are ahead of their Nations League clash against the Czech Republic.

Both Merino and Zubimendi were also keen to stress that they will be looking to gain more opportunities and not get distracted.

Merino has had to adapt to his new role at Arsenal after playing a key role on his team’s side. However, Merino has struggled to get into the starting XI.

He admitted that he wants to play more games. However, he acknowledged that it was difficult to get into the team, as there are so many quality players.

This shows that his playing time has not affected his relationship with Arteta.

Merino was able to understand what it is like to be a manager because his father was a football coach. He understands that tough decisions have to be made when selecting your starting XI.

This can be an important aspect in a difficult season, as all players need to play their part to make sure Arsenal stay challenging in multiple competitions.

Merino’s comments are very interesting considering the uncertainty around Zubimendi.

There are reports Zubimendi has been linked to Atletico Madrid and whether he will be looking to move in January.

Merino didn’t give a definite answer that these players will stay at Arsenal, but the comments do suggest they are looking to improve their position in the squad.

He also underlined the importance of having good cover, with Spain boss Luis de la Fuente believing players coming off the bench can be just as vital as those starting.

This is something Arsenal will want their squad to take on board. They will not always be able to play the same midfielders due to the demands of playing in both domestic and European competitions.

There is still time for Merino and Zubimendi to turn their situation around, so what they are doing now may not indicate how important they are going to be in the campaign.

Arsenal will be keen to keep Merino happy, and he has made his position clear. This should give some reassurance ahead of the January transfer window.

#2133. Birmingham City's Powerhouse plans could change as club announce fan action

Birmingham City supporters have plenty of good reasons to be excited right now, with Chris Davies' side topping the Championship for the first time in many years, coupled with the well-documented plans set out by Knighthead.

Blues' American investors have completely changed the mood around St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park, and in a matter of years, such ambition is leading to a change of environment.

Having been mooted in April 2024, Birmingham unveiled the name and design of their planned 62,000-seater stadium a year ago this week.

The Powerhouse will pay tribute to the Second City's industrious past whilst being the centrepiece of the Sports Quarter regeneration project.

During the planning stages, Blues' owners have got many high-profile names on board regarding key elements such as transport, the creation of jobs and how the stadium will look on the outside and inside.

One figure constantly associated with the Sports Quarter development beyond Tom Wagner is Nick Smith, who became Birmingham's head of infrastructure in 2023.

Smith has issued several updates surrounding the planned development, which is set to be completed in the summer of 2031.

He, along with other Blues chiefs, have been in constant dialogue with supporters over the stadium move, as seen in April where he and Heatherwick Studio's Eliot Postma explained its scale at an event named 'Built by Us'.

With Thursday November 20th being the one-year anniversary of the Powerhouse's unveiling, Smith announced last week that another fan-led consultation will go live, titled 'Shaped by You'.

The concept will see Smith send out one question regarding the Powerhouse, to which Bluenoses have five days to respond, before feedback is detailed amongst relevant staff to help shape the experience into one which will be enjoyed by the entire fanbase.

Whilst the 12-chimney design has led to mixed reviews, it is one which will certainly be staying, but that doesn't mean there haven't been changes made in recent times to the overall Sports Quarter.

Indeed, it was recently confirmed that Birmingham are looking for a new patch of land to build training facilities which will house all of the club's men's, women's and academy sides under one roof, as well as a separate stadium for the women's team.

Birmingham City can seal their return to the Premier League by revisiting a move for Portsmouth star Adrian Segecic in January

The Sports Quarter is set to take up 135 acres of land, with reports detailing that the planned training facilities were set to take up over a half of such land, making it unfeasible.

This idea was heavily backed by Football League World's Birmingham City fan pundit, Jason Moore.

Compared to previous ownership regimes at St. Andrew's, few can fault the lengths at which Knighthead are going to in order to make supporters feel engaged with all that comes along with supporting Blues.

There have been several 'Open House' forums which have detailed goings-on on the pitch as well as administratively, and 'Shaped by You' isn't the only campaign which has been launched this month.

Blues fans, what needs to be considered the most ahead of the Powerhouse stadium move? Comment below!

Blues confirmed a new brand campaign ahead of the 3-0 win against Millwall on November 3rd titled 'Unreasonable', fronted by supporter and actor, Jayden Healey, who explained the concept.

"Is it unreasonable to believe that we can have a 62,000-seater stadium, be the biggest club in the world and play Champions League football? Yeah, that's the point of it. But, I believe we're going to get there," he said.

#2131. Two days or two weeks – Michael Carrick future decision rolls into the international break

Manchester United will use the November international break to decide whether Michael Carrick stays on as head coach, after a three-game reprieve that delivered only one win.

According to The Guardian, Carrick came close to being sacked after the 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth on 25 October.

Director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada discussed his position at the training ground the following day and agreed to give him three matches to turn things around before the break.

Those games brought a 2-0 defeat at Chelsea, a 3-2 win over Roma and a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday. United conceded eight goals across the three fixtures, and defensive frailty remains the biggest worry.

Wilcox is now leading a review of Carrick’s position. He will consult Berrada before making a recommendation to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who oversees the club’s sporting operations. Talks are expected to begin on Monday and continue through the break.

The league table makes grim reading. United sit in the Premier League relegation zone with just one league win in their last 10 matches.

If he does win a stay of execution, results will need to follow. Manchester United cannot be languishing in 17th place.

Carrick remains defiant. Speaking to Sky Sports News after the Villa draw, he admitted his side “haven’t won enough games” but insisted he expects to move forward.

“I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games, said Carrick after the late Villa draw.

“I think there’s more than enough [to turn things around].”

If United do make a change, former Newcastle manager Eddie Howe is reported to be Wilcox’s preferred candidate. Howe has been out of work since leaving St James’ Park during pre-season, after four and a half years in charge.

In the meantime, there are no plans to strengthen Carrick’s coaching staff.

For now, Carrick is expected to be in charge for United’s next match, against Liverpool. Whether three games were enough to convince the hierarchy should become clear before then.

The trip to Anfield could be do or die for the decorated former United midfielder.

He’s not likely to survive a heavy defeat at the home of the club’s fierce rivals, but a galvanising win would surely buy him time and goodwill.

That’s if he makes it through the next fortnight before then. A decision or indication could be two days or two weeks away.

The only certainty at Old Trafford is uncertainty.

#2129. Chelsea World Cup Knockout Load Gives Xabi Alonso Pre-Season Problem

Chelsea’s World Cup contingent has moved from a group-stage watchlist into a genuine Xabi Alonso planning problem.

Chelsea’s own tournament update confirms that Enzo Fernandez, Mike Penders, Moises Caicedo, Kendry Paez, Malo Gusto and Jorrel Hato have reached the Round of 32.

England have also progressed after their final Group L win over Panama, which keeps Reece James and Trevoh Chalobah inside the wider knockout picture.

For supporters, that is a status marker. For Alonso, it is where summer pride starts to become pre-season compression.

The concern is not simply volume. It is where the minutes are landing.

Enzo has not missed a minute for Argentina, while Caicedo has remained central for Ecuador and captained them in the 2-1 win over Germany.

Those are not fringe workloads. They are the two midfield profiles Chelsea have built large parts of their control game around.

Alonso’s first Chelsea pre-season was always going to demand clarity through the middle of the pitch.

Instead, the players most central to that reset are still operating in knockout football.

Caicedo’s Ecuador role is the cleanest example. Read Chelsea has already assessed how his captaincy display against Germany strengthened his leadership case, but the next layer is more complicated.

Every additional knockout tie gives him more tournament rhythm, more authority and more fatigue.

Argentina’s route against Cape Verde keeps him on a glamorous stage at exactly the moment Chelsea need to settle his role, mood and tactical responsibilities under Alonso.

If Madrid-related noise continues around him, the club cannot afford a sluggish July handover.

Reece James started England’s first two matches before a hamstring issue ruled him out of the Panama game, according to the Guardian.

England still topped the group and moved into a last-32 tie with DR Congo, but James’ situation is exactly the kind of detail Chelsea’s medical team will monitor closely.

Chelsea have already had to plan around a large World Cup group.

The broader issue was clear in Read Chelsea’s earlier pre-season workload piece, but the knockout stage sharpens it because the returns will now be staggered.

Enzo brings a maximum group-stage load. Caicedo brings captaincy responsibility and heavy Ecuador minutes.

James brings knockout qualification mixed with another hamstring-management question.

Gusto and Hato remain tied to France and the Netherlands, while Penders and Paez are still absorbing tournament environments before club reintegration.

That is a spine issue, not a fringe issue.

Alonso needs automatisms in possession, spacing around the double pivot, clearer full-back behaviour and pressing triggers from midfield.

Those details do not bed in properly when key players arrive in drips after a major summer tournament.

Players returning from knockout football can bring competitive sharpness that closed-door friendlies cannot replicate.

Caicedo captaining Ecuador through pressure games matters. Enzo playing high-leverage minutes for Argentina matters.

Gusto and Hato absorbing tournament detail also helps Chelsea’s defensive reset.

But Chelsea cannot treat every tournament minute as clean preparation.

Alonso must decide who returns straight into tactical work, who needs a genuine pause and who can handle August without creating an avoidable injury bill by September.

That is where the James situation feels central.

If Chelsea’s captain carries a World Cup hamstring warning, the club’s right-sided structure becomes more than a selection debate.

It becomes an availability question that touches Gusto, the wider defensive rebuild and the need for control from midfield.

Read Chelsea has already looked at James’ captaincy test under Alonso, and the injury layer now makes that test sharper.

This is the hidden cost of a strong international footprint.

Chelsea want players good enough to survive deep into tournaments.

Alonso now has to make sure that status does not leave his first league weeks short of the very control those players are meant to provide.
